definition_zh: 主席；董事长；会议主持人
definition_en: the person who leads a meeting, a committee or a company
core_image: 坐在长桌首席、掌控全场节奏的那个人
scene: 年会开始时，众人安静下来等他上台。 The chairman opened the meeting.
sceneCN: 这里 chairman 指「主席」（第 1 个义项：会议的主持人）；句意是主席宣布会议开始。

senses.title: The leader of a meeting
senses.definition: the person who controls the order of a meeting and keeps it on time
senses.definitionCN: 掌控会议程序、使会议按时进行的人
senses.example: The chairman asked for a vote.
senses.exampleCN: 主席要求进行表决。
senses.why: The word joins chair, the leader seat, to man, so it names the person who occupies that seat.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把表示领导座位的 chair 与 man 结合，指占据那个座位的人。

senses.title: The head of a company
senses.definition: the most senior officer who leads the board of a company
senses.definitionCN: 领导公司董事会的最高负责人
senses.example: The chairman announced the merger.
senses.exampleCN: 董事长宣布了合并。
senses.why: A board is led from the same head seat, so the title travels from the meeting room into the company.
senses.whyCN: 董事会同样由首席之座来领导，于是这个头衔从会议室走进了公司。

intro.en: Chairman pairs the seat of authority with the old word for a person, and English has used it since the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: chairman 把权威座位与古老的「人」一词配在一起，英语自十七世纪起使用它。

items.en: Cathedra named a formal seat of authority.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cathedra 指权威的正式座位。

items.en: Old French chaire gave English the word chair.
items.cn: 古法语 chaire 给英语提供了 chair 一词。

items.en: English chair names the furniture and later the leading seat.
items.cn: 十三世纪英语 chair 指家具，后来指领导之位。

items.en: Chairman appears for the person who presides over a meeting.
items.cn: 十七世纪出现 chairman，指主持会议的人。

items.en: The word spreads from meetings to committees and boards of companies.
items.cn: 这个词从会议扩展到委员会与公司董事会。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the chair compounds, while the meaning group lists other heads of an organization.
note.cn: 形近组收集 chair 的复合词，近义组列出其他机构负责人。

entries.definition: the leading seat or office
a woman who leads a meeting
a neutral word for the leader
the head of a company or country
entries.definitionCN: 公司或国家的最高负责人

entries.definition: a senior member of a board
the person in charge of a group

normalIntro.en: These hooks read the word as the man in the chair and attach the boardroom phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把词读成「坐在那把椅子上的人」，并挂上董事会的搭配。

normal.en: Break it as chair plus man: the man who holds the chair runs the meeting.
normal.cn: 拆成 chair 加 man：握着主席之位的人掌控会议。

normal.en: The chairman of the board sits above the directors.
normal.cn: the chairman of the board 位于各位董事之上。

normal.en: Vice chairman and acting chairman mark the second and the temporary holder.
normal.cn: vice chairman 与 acting chairman 分别标记副手与临时代理。

normal.en: To elect a chairman is to pick who will sit at the head of the table.
normal.cn: elect a chairman 就是选出谁坐长桌首席。

normal.en: Chairmanship is the office and its term, not the person.
normal.cn: chairmanship 指职位与任期，而不是那个人。

abstract.en: Picture one hand tapping the table to call for order.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手敲桌面，要求全场安静。

abstract.en: Picture a name plate at the head of a long table.
abstract.cn: 想象长桌首席摆着一块名牌。

abstract.en: Picture a room falling silent when one person stands.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站起时整间屋子静下来。

examples.en: The chairman called for silence.
examples.cn: 主席请大家安静。

examples.en: He was elected chairman of the committee.
examples.cn: 他被选为委员会主席。

examples.en: The chairman and the directors met at noon.
examples.cn: 董事长与董事们中午会面。

dict_mnemonic.text: chair 是那把首席椅子，man 是人：坐在首席上的人就是主席。

root: 由 chair（座位、主席职位）加 man（人）构成，chair 源自拉丁语 cathedra。

sensesIntro.en: The meeting leader is the earlier sense, and the same word extends to the head of a company board.
sensesIntro.cn: 会议主持人义出现较早，同一个词又扩展到公司董事会的负责人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the person seated at the head of the table.
core.cn: 核心意象：坐在长桌首席的那个人。

branches.en: The meeting sense keeps the live job of running a session.
branches.cn: 会议义保留主持一场会议的实际工作。

branches.en: The company sense widens the role to a board.
branches.cn: 公司义把这一角色扩大到董事会。

branches.en: Both depend on one person holding the leading seat.
branches.cn: 两者都依赖一个人占据领导之座。

branches.en: Voting and keeping order belong to the meeting sense.
branches.cn: 表决与维持秩序属于会议义。

branches.en: Board meetings and mergers belong to the company sense.
branches.cn: 董事会与合并属于公司义。

intro.en: Chairman builds chairmanship and pairs with vice and acting, while chairperson offers a neutral form.
intro.cn: chairman 构成 chairmanship，并与 vice、acting 搭配，chairperson 则提供中性形式。

latinIntro.en: The chair inside the word descends from Latin cathedra, a seat of authority.
latinIntro.cn: 词中的 chair 源自拉丁语 cathedra，即权威之座。

items.meaning: the leader of a meeting or board
items.meaningCN: 会议或董事会的领导者

items.exampleCN: 他的主席任期持续了五年。

latinEntries.example: Sedes also meant a seat in Latin.
latinEntries.exampleCN: sedes 在拉丁语中也指座位。

definition_zh: 承诺；投入；犯（错误或罪行）；托付
definition_en: to promise firmly to do something, to do something wrong, or to give your time and effort fully to something
core_image: 把自己整个人押在一件事上，不再回头
scene: 他在合同上签下名字，答应投入整整两年。 She committed herself to the project for two years.
sceneCN: 这里 commit 指「承诺；投入」（第 1 个义项：下定决心去做）；句意是她承诺为这个项目投入两年。

senses.title: To promise firmly
senses.definition: to decide to do something and give it your full effort
senses.definitionCN: 下定决心去做某事并全力以赴
senses.example: She committed herself to the project for two years.
senses.exampleCN: 她承诺为这个项目投入两年。
senses.why: To commit is to hand yourself over, and a promise does exactly that.
senses.whyCN: commit 就是把自己交出去，而承诺做的正是这件事。

senses.title: To do something wrong
senses.definition: to carry out a crime, a mistake or a foolish act
senses.definitionCN: 做出罪行、错误或愚蠢的举动
senses.example: He committed a serious error in the report.
senses.exampleCN: 他在报告里犯了一个严重的错误。
senses.why: A wrong act is also something you hand over to the record, so the word is used for crimes.
senses.whyCN: 错事同样是你交给记录的东西，因此这个词也用于犯罪。

senses.title: To send for treatment
senses.definition: to order someone to be kept in a hospital or prison
senses.definitionCN: 下令把某人送进医院或监狱
senses.example: The judge committed him to prison for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 法官判他入狱一年。
senses.why: The old sense of handing a person over survives in courts and hospitals.
senses.whyCN: 把人交出去的古老含义在法庭与医院里留存下来。

intro.en: Commit comes from Latin committere, to bring together or entrust.
intro.cn: commit 来自拉丁语 committere，意为把事物合在一起或托付出去。

items.en: Committere joined com-, together, with mittere, to send.
items.cn: committere 把表示一起的 com- 与表示送出的 mittere 结合。

items.en: It described handing a person or task into another's charge.
items.cn: 它描述把人或任务交到别人手中。

items.en: Old French commettre kept the sense of entrusting and of doing wrong.
items.cn: 古法语 commettre 兼具托付与做错事两种含义。

items.en: English commit covered both handing over and carrying out an act.
items.cn: 英语 commit 既指交出，也指实施某个行为。

items.en: The modern word centres on promises, effort and wrongdoing.
items.cn: 现代英语中它聚焦于承诺、投入与过失。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words shaped like commit, while the meaning group lists verbs of promising and devoting.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 commit 形状相近的短词，近义组列出承诺与投入的动词。

entries.definition: fighting between armed forces
an icy body that moves around the sun
to agree that something is true
to promise seriously to do something
to give time and effort to a cause
entries.definitionCN: 把时间与精力献给某事

entries.definition: to carry out a crime or harmful act

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with signing away your own time, then move to wrong acts and to being handed into a prison.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从签下自己的时间开始，再走到错事与被送进监狱。

normal.en: Commit is to send yourself into something with no way back.
normal.cn: commit 就是把自己送进去，不留退路。

normal.en: The doubled t appears in committed and committing, but not in commit.
normal.cn: committed 与 committing 双写 t，但 commit 本身不双写。

normal.en: You commit a crime or an error, and you commit to a person or plan.
normal.cn: 你犯下罪行或错误，也把自己承诺给某个人或计划。

normal.en: Commit to memory means sending a fact into lasting storage.
normal.cn: 牢记就是把一个事实送进长期存储。

normal.en: A committed teacher gives more than the timetable asks.
normal.cn: 一位尽心尽力的老师，付出的比课表要求的多。

abstract.en: Picture a signature pressed hard enough to mark the page below.
abstract.cn: 想象签名用力到在下一页留下印痕。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy door closing behind a person.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇沉重的门在人身后关上。

abstract.en: Picture a candle burning at only one end, deliberately.
abstract.cn: 想象一支蜡烛被刻意只在一头燃烧。

examples.en: He committed himself to training every morning.
examples.cn: 他坚持每天早上训练。

examples.en: The clerk committed a small error in the list.
examples.cn: 职员在名单上犯了个小错。

examples.en: They committed the old files to memory.
examples.cn: 他们把旧档案牢牢记住。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 commit 记成 com（一起）加 mit（送出）：把自己整个送出去，就是承诺与投入。

root: 源自拉丁语 committere，com- 表示一起，mittere 表示送出，本义是交出去、托付，后引申为承诺投入与犯错。

sensesIntro.en: From handing yourself over to a task, to handing a wrong act to the record, and to handing a person into custody.
sensesIntro.cn: 从把自己交给一项任务，到把错事交给记录，再到把人交入监管。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: staking your whole self on one thing with no way back.
core.cn: 核心意象：把自己整个人押在一件事上，不再回头。

branches.en: The promise sense is the everyday modern one.
branches.cn: 承诺义是现代最日常的义项。

branches.en: A crime is an act handed over to the record.
branches.cn: 罪行就是被交给记录的行为。

branches.en: Courts still use the old sense of handing a person over.
branches.cn: 法庭至今仍用「把人交出去」这个古老义项。

branches.en: Both a promise and a crime are acts you cannot easily undo.
branches.cn: 承诺与罪行都是不易撤回的行为。

branches.en: Devotion and custody both begin with a transfer of control.
branches.cn: 投入与收押都始于控制权的转移。

intro.en: Commit builds nouns with -ment and -al, and its past forms double the final t.
intro.cn: commit 用 -ment 与 -al 构成名词，过去式与分词双写词尾的 t。

latinIntro.en: The Latin mittere, to send, also appears in mission, permit and submit.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mittere（送出）也出现在 mission、permit 与 submit 之中。

items.meaning: promises, or does a wrong act
items.example: He commits one hour a day to reading.
items.exampleCN: 他每天拿出一小时读书。

items.meaning: gave full effort or carried out an act
items.example: They committed more money to the plan.

items.meaning: the act of promising or doing wrong
items.example: She is committing too much time to one task.

这份工作需要真正的投入。

items.example: He has family commitments this weekend.

items.meaning: the act of sending someone to prison or court
items.example: The committal hearing lasted an hour.
items.exampleCN: 交付审理的听证持续了一小时。

items.structure: related noun from the same root
items.meaning: a task or authority entrusted to someone

items.structure: related noun from the same root

definition_zh: 弹跳；上下晃动；（支票）被退回
definition_en: to hit a surface and spring back up
core_image: 球撞墙后弹回
scene: 球从墙上弹了回来。 The ball bounced off the wall.
sceneCN: 这里 bounce 是「弹跳」（第 1 个义项：撞到表面后反弹回来）；句意是球从墙上弹了回来。

collocations.zh: 支票因余额不足被退回

derivatives.zh: 夜店保安；弹跳力强的人

senses.title: To spring back from a surface
senses.definition: to hit something and move away from it quickly
senses.definitionCN: 撞到某物后迅速离开
senses.example: The ball bounced off the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 球从墙上弹了回来。
senses.why: This is the core sense, from an old word for a heavy blow.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心义项，来自古时表示重击的词。

senses.title: To move up and down
senses.definition: to move up and down again and again
senses.definitionCN: 反复地上下移动
senses.example: The children bounced on the bed.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在床上蹦来蹦去。
senses.why: Anything springing on a soft surface repeats the same movement.
senses.whyCN: 柔软表面上的弹起会不断重复同一个动作。

senses.title: To be sent back unpaid
senses.definition: to be returned by a bank because there is no money
senses.definitionCN: 因账户无钱被银行退回
senses.example: His cheque bounced at the bank.
senses.exampleCN: 他的支票被银行退回了。
senses.why: A cheque that springs back to the payer is said to bounce.
senses.whyCN: 支票弹回付款人手里，就说它 bounce 了。

intro.en: Bounce first meant to beat or thump, and the springing sense came later.
intro.cn: bounce 最初意为击打，反弹义出现得较晚。

items.en: bunsen meant to beat or thump.
items.cn: bunsen 意为击打或重捶。

items.en: bounce named a heavy blow.
items.cn: bounce 指重重的一击。

items.en: bounce meant to spring back from a surface.
items.cn: bounce 指从表面弹回。

items.en: a bounced cheque was returned unpaid.
items.cn: bounced cheque 指被退回的支票。

items.en: bounce covers springing, jumping and returns.
items.cn: 如今 bounce 兼指反弹、蹦跳与退回。

note.en: The look-alike group rhymes with bounce; the near-meaning group names springing movements.
note.cn: 形近组与 bounce 押韵；近义组是弹起的动作。

normalIntro.cn: bounce 就是不肯停在地上的球。

normal.en: Bounce and bounced are the base and past forms.

normal.en: A ball bounces off a wall.

normal.en: Bounce back means to recover.

normal.en: Bouncy means full of spring.

root: bounce 源自中古英语 bunsen（击打），十六世纪指重击，十九世纪转为撞后弹回，二十世纪又指支票被退回。

items.meaning: a person who guards a club door

definition_zh: 非正式的；随意的；口语化的；不拘礼节的
definition_en: not formal or official, or relaxed and friendly in style and manner
core_image: 脱掉西装的会面：不用拘礼，怎么舒服怎么来
scene: 周五傍晚，同事们抱着咖啡杯在沙发上围坐一圈聊工作。 We had an informal discussion about the project over coffee.
sceneCN: 这里 informal 是「非正式的」（第 1 个义项：不遵循正式程序的）；句意：我们边喝咖啡边对项目进行了非正式讨论。

collocations.zh: 随意的文风；非正式文体

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「非正式地；随意地」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「非正式；不拘礼节」
去掉否定前缀所得的反义词，义为「正式的」
名词形式，指非正式的状态

senses.title: Not following official rules or procedures
senses.titleCN: 非正式的；不循官方程序的
senses.definition: not arranged or recognized according to official rules
senses.definitionCN: 未按官方规章安排或认可的
senses.example: They settled the dispute through an informal agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 他们通过一份非正式协议解决了争端。
senses.why: The negative prefix in- simply cancels the officialness carried by formal.
senses.whyCN: 否定前缀 in- 直接取消了 formal 所带的「官方、规范」意味。

senses.title: Relaxed and friendly in manner
senses.definition: relaxed, friendly, and not stiff in behavior or dress
senses.definitionCN: 举止或穿着放松、友善、不拘谨的
senses.example: The party had an informal, cheerful atmosphere.
senses.exampleCN: 聚会的氛围轻松随意、气氛欢快。
senses.why: What is not formal naturally feels loose and warm.
senses.whyCN: 不属于正式场合的东西，自然显得松弛而亲切。

senses.title: Used in everyday speech rather than writing
senses.definition: suitable for conversation but not for official or academic writing
senses.definitionCN: 适合口语而不适合正式或学术书面语的
senses.example: Kids is an informal word for children.
senses.exampleCN: kids 是 children 的口语说法。
senses.why: Spoken language drops ceremony just as casual dress drops a jacket.
senses.whyCN: 口语卸掉客套，就像休闲装脱掉西装外套。

intro.en: Informal is a late Latin formation: the negative prefix in- attached to formalis.
intro.cn: informal 是晚期拉丁语的构词：否定前缀 in- 加到 formalis 之上。

items.en: Latin formalis meant formal, shaped, derived from forma (shape).
items.cn: 拉丁语 formalis 意为「正式的；有形状的」，派生自 forma（形状）。

items.en: Late Latin produced informalis by adding the negative prefix in-.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语加上否定前缀 in-，造出 informalis。

items.en: English formed informal in the seventeenth century, first about outward shape and ceremony.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪造出 informal，最初用于形容外形与礼仪。

items.en: The relaxed-manner sense spread in the nineteenth century as social life loosened.
items.cn: 十九世纪随社交生活松绑，「随意」义广泛传播。

items.en: Linguistics later fixed the spoken-language sense for register description.
items.cn: 语言学后来将「口语语体」义固定下来，用于语域描述。

note.en: The family all hangs on forma; the meaning neighbors describe loose style.
note.cn: 词族都挂在 forma 上；近义词描述松散风格。

entries.definition: following official or ceremonial rules
entries.definitionCN: 正式的；informal 的直接反义词

definition_zh: 顾问；指导者；导师（亦拼作 advisor）
definition_en: a person whose job is to give expert advice, or someone who guides another person's studies or decisions
core_image: 一个人站在你侧后方半步，看着同一份文件替你圈出重点
scene: 学生把选课表摊在桌上，几门课的时间撞在一起，家长也拿不定主意。 Her academic adviser helped her rearrange the timetable.
sceneCN: 这里 adviser 指学校里负责指导学生学业的老师（第 2 个义项：学业导师）；句意为她的学业导师帮她重新排了课表。

forms.label: 异体拼写 advisor 的复数

derivatives.zh: 由同源动词 advise 加后缀 -ory 构成，义为「顾问的；咨询的」
由本词加名词后缀 -ship 构成，义为「顾问职位；顾问身份」

senses.title: A professional consultant
senses.definition: a person whose job is to give expert advice to a company, a government or an individual
senses.definitionCN: 以向公司、政府或个人提供专业意见为职业的人
senses.example: The firm hired an adviser to review its energy costs.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司聘请了一位顾问来审查能源开支。
senses.why: The French verb aviser means to form a view, and the agent suffix -er names the person who does it as a job, so an adviser is the one paid to look and judge.
senses.whyCN: 法语动词 aviser 意为「形成看法」，施事后缀 -er 指以这件事为业的人，所以 adviser 是受雇去看、去判断的那个人。

senses.title: An academic guide
senses.definition: a teacher at a school or university who helps a student choose courses and plan their studies
senses.definitionCN: 学校里帮助学生选课、规划学业的老师
senses.example: Her academic adviser suggested dropping one of the two science courses.
senses.exampleCN: 她的学业导师建议她退掉两门理科课中的一门。
senses.why: In a university the same role narrows to study: the person looks at a student's path and points out the next step.
senses.whyCN: 在大学里，同一个角色缩小到学业上：这个人看着学生的路径，指出下一步该往哪走。

senses.title: Anyone who offers advice
senses.definition: a person, often trusted or senior, who gives another person advice without holding a formal post
senses.definitionCN: 不担任正式职务、却为他人出主意的人，往往是受信任者或长辈
senses.example: Throughout the crisis he remained her closest adviser.
senses.exampleCN: 整个危机期间，他始终是她最亲近的谋士。
senses.why: No job title is needed: whoever is looked to for a view becomes an adviser for that moment.
senses.whyCN: 不需要任何头衔：谁被当成可以拿主意的人，谁在那个时刻就是 adviser。

intro.en: Adviser is the agent noun of the French verb that also gave English advise, and its two spellings reflect two different endings.
intro.cn: adviser 是那个同时带来英语 advise 的法语动词的施事名词，它的两种拼写来自两个不同的词尾。

items.en: Latin videre 'to see' and its participle visum 'what is seen' lie behind the French word; the combination with ad is generally assumed, though the exact derivation is not certain.
items.cn: 拉丁语 videre「看见」及其分词 visum「所见之物」是法语词的底子；与 ad 的结合一般认为成立，但确切构成并不确定。

items.en: The verb aviser meant to consider and to give an opinion, and from it English took both the verb advise and the idea of the person who advises.
items.cn: 动词 aviser 意为「思量、提出看法」，英语由它既取来动词 advise，也取来「提出看法的人」这一概念。

items.en: English added the native agent suffix -er to the borrowed verb, giving adviser for the person who gives the view.
items.cn: 英语给借来的动词加上本土施事后缀 -er，得到 adviser，指提出看法的人。

items.en: A second spelling, advisor, was formed with the Latin-looking ending -or. Both forms have been in use since the sixteenth century and mean exactly the same thing.
items.cn: 另一种拼写 advisor 用看起来像拉丁语的词尾 -or 构成。两种形式自十六世纪起并用，含义完全相同。

items.en: Adviser is the usual form in British edited prose, while advisor is common in American job titles and organization names; dictionaries treat them as variants, not as different words.
items.cn: 在英国编辑体例中 adviser 更常见，而 advisor 多用于美式职位头衔与机构名称；词典把二者视为异体拼写，而非两个不同的词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the variant spelling and the words built on the same verb; the near-meaning group gathers other people who give guidance, with different degrees of formality.
note.cn: 形近组收异体拼写与同一动词构成的词；近义组收其他提供指导的人，正式程度各不相同。

entries.definition: The same noun spelled with the Latin-looking ending -or, common in job titles and organization names.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，adviser 的另一种拼写，词尾用看起来像拉丁语的 -or，多见于职位头衔与机构名称，读音和含义完全相同。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to give someone advice; the person who does this is the adviser.
entries.definitionCN: 同源动词，义为「建议、劝告」；执行这个动作的人就是 adviser。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning having the role of giving advice, or a noun for a body that does so.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「顾问的、咨询的」；作名词时指提供咨询的机构。

entries.definition: The noun for the opinion itself, ending in c and pronounced with /s/.
entries.definitionCN: 同源名词，指意见本身，以 c 结尾、读清音 /s/，与指人的 adviser 分工不同。

entries.definition: An expert who is paid by a company to advise on a particular field.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「咨询顾问」，指受公司聘请、就某一领域提供意见的专家，职业色彩比 adviser 更强。

entries.definition: A formal word for a legal adviser or for the advice itself.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「法律顾问」或「忠告」，语气正式，法律色彩明显。

entries.definition: An experienced person who guides someone over a long period, usually in work or life rather than in one case.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「导师、引路人」，指长期指导他人的人，多在工作或人生层面，而非处理单个案子。

entries.definition: A person who shows the way, literally or figuratively; broader and less technical than adviser.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「向导、指导者」，可实指带路的人，也可比喻，范围比 adviser 宽，专业色彩更弱。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real French verb, the agent suffix, and the phrases in which this person noun appears.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子依据真实的法语动词、施事后缀，以及这个指人的名词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: advise plus -er gives the person who gives the view.
normal.cn: advise 加 -er，就得到给出看法的那个人。

normal.en: Adviser and advisor are one word with two endings: -er is the English agent suffix, -or the Latin-looking one.
normal.cn: adviser 与 advisor 是同一个词的两种词尾：-er 是英语施事后缀，-or 是看起来像拉丁语的词尾。

normal.en: An academic adviser handles courses; a financial adviser handles money.
normal.cn: academic adviser 管选课，financial adviser 管钱。

normal.en: Adviser to the president shows that the role is tied to a person in power.
normal.cn: adviser to the president 说明这个角色依附于掌权者。

normal.en: A consultant is usually hired by a firm, while an adviser may be a trusted friend.
normal.cn: consultant 通常由公司聘用，而 adviser 也可能是身边受信任的朋友。

abstract.en: Picture someone standing half a step behind you, looking at the same page and circling the lines that matter.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在你侧后方半步，和你看同一页纸，把要紧的几行圈出来。

abstract.en: The adviser does not carry the bag or walk the road; the adviser only makes the map easier to read.
abstract.cn: 顾问不替你背包，也不替你走路；他只是让地图更好读。

abstract.en: The same figure can sit in a palace, a clinic or a dormitory: the setting changes, the half step behind does not.
abstract.cn: 同一个人物可以出现在宫殿、诊所或宿舍：场景变了，那半步的距离不变。

examples.en: The company's legal adviser reviewed the contract.
examples.cn: 公司的法律顾问审阅了这份合同。

examples.en: Academic advisers help students choose their courses.
examples.cn: 学业导师帮助学生选课。

examples.en: She served as an adviser to two mayors.
examples.cn: 她曾担任两任市长的顾问。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德外泽」——阿德站在你侧后方，替你圈出文件上的重点：顾问。

root: 由古法语动词 aviser「思量、提出看法」加英语施事后缀 -er 构成；avis 一般认为出自拉丁语 ad「朝向」+ videre「看」。异体拼写 advisor 借了拉丁语风格的词尾 -or。

sensesIntro.en: The three senses all name the same figure: someone who looks at a situation and points out a way, whether as a paid expert, a study guide, or a trusted voice.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项都指同一种人：看清局势后指出一条路的人，只是身份不同——受聘的专家、学业上的导师，或身边受信任的进言者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person half a step behind you, looking at the same page and circling what matters.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在你侧后方半步，和你看着同一页纸，把要紧处圈出来。

branches.en: THE PROFESSION: expert looking is sold as a service to firms and governments.
branches.cn: 职业线：专家的「看」被当作服务，卖给公司与政府。

branches.en: THE CAMPUS: the same looking narrows to courses and study plans.
branches.cn: 校园线：同样的「看」缩小到选课与学习计划上。

branches.en: THE INFORMAL VOICE: no post is needed, only the trust of the person being advised.
branches.cn: 非正式线：不需要职位，只需要被建议者的信任。

branches.en: TRUST IS THE COMMON CORE: paid or unpaid, the adviser is the one whose view is asked for.
branches.cn: 信任是共同内核：无论受聘与否，顾问都是那个被征询看法的人。

branches.en: ONE ROLE, THREE SETTINGS: office, campus and kitchen table all hold the same half step behind.
branches.cn: 一个角色，三处场景：办公室、校园与厨房餐桌旁，都站着同一个「半步之后」的人。

intro.en: Adviser is a borrowed French verb plus an English agent suffix; the second spelling simply swaps in a Latin-looking ending.
intro.cn: adviser 是借来的法语动词加英语施事后缀；另一种拼写只是换了一个看起来像拉丁语的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre and visum are recorded, and ad is a recorded preposition; the French verb aviser is also recorded, while the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre 与 visum 均有记录，ad 也是有记录的介词；法语动词 aviser 同样有记录，更早的印欧词根则属重构形式。

definition_zh: 橱柜；内阁；陈列室
definition_en: a piece of furniture with shelves or drawers for storing things
core_image: 靠墙立着的带门储物柜
scene: 厨房里碗碟都收在柜中。 She put the plates back in the cabinet.
sceneCN: 这里 cabinet 是「橱柜」（第 1 个义项：带门和隔板的储物家具）；句意是她把盘子放回橱柜。

derivatives.zh: 橱柜制作工艺，也指整套橱柜

senses.title: A storage cupboard
senses.definition: a piece of furniture with doors and shelves for keeping things
senses.definitionCN: 带门和隔板、用来存放物品的家具
senses.example: She put the plates back in the cabinet.
senses.exampleCN: 她把盘子放回橱柜。
senses.why: The core image is a closed wooden box standing against a wall.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一只靠墙立着的封闭木柜。

senses.title: The senior ministers of a government
senses.definition: the group of senior ministers who advise a head of government
senses.definitionCN: 为政府首脑提供建议的高级部长群体
senses.example: The cabinet met to discuss the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 内阁开会讨论预算。
senses.why: Ministers once met in a small private room, and the room's name passed to the group.
senses.whyCN: 部长们曾在一间小密室里议事，房间的名字就转指这群人。

senses.title: A small room for display
senses.definition: a small room used to display objects or keep a collection
senses.definitionCN: 用来陈列物品或收藏品的小房间
senses.example: The coin cabinet is upstairs.
senses.exampleCN: 钱币陈列室在楼上。
senses.why: The older sense was a small private room, later used for showing collections.
senses.whyCN: 较早的意思是私密小房间，后来用于展出收藏品。

intro.en: Cabinet began as a small room and later named the furniture in it.
intro.cn: cabinet 最初指小房间，后来指房间里的家具。

items.en: cabinet was a diminutive of cabine, a small room.
items.cn: 古法语 cabinet 是 cabine 的指小形式，意为小房间。

items.en: English cabinet named a private room for valuables.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语 cabinet 指存放贵重物品的私室。

items.en: The word shifted to the chest of drawers kept there.
items.cn: 十七世纪词义转向放在那里的抽屉柜。

items.en: Cabinet named the advisers meeting in a private room.
items.cn: 十八世纪 cabinet 指在私室议事的顾问团。

items.en: Cabinet covers cupboards, government advisers and display rooms.
items.cn: 现代英语中 cabinet 兼指橱柜、政府内阁与陈列室。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cabin base; the near-meaning group gives other storage furniture.
note.cn: 形近组共用 cabin 词基；近义组是其他储物家具。

a small wooden house or room
a piece of furniture with shelves and doors
a small locked cupboard for personal things
a tall cupboard for clothes

normalIntro.en: Cabinet moved from a room to the furniture and then to a government group.
normalIntro.cn: cabinet 从小房间转到家具，再转到政府班子。

normal.en: The plural is cabinets.
normal.cn: 复数是 cabinets。

normal.en: A filing cabinet holds documents.
normal.cn: filing cabinet 存放文件。

normal.en: A cabinet meeting is held by ministers.
normal.cn: cabinet meeting 由部长们召开。

normal.en: Cabinetry is the craft of making cabinets.
normal.cn: cabinetry 指橱柜制作工艺。

normal.en: The word is related to cabin.

abstract.en: See a wall of doors opening onto neat shelves.
abstract.cn: 想象一整墙柜门打开，露出整齐的隔板。

abstract.en: See a small room with a heavy table and closed doors.
abstract.cn: 想象一间小室，里面一张厚桌，门关着。

abstract.en: See coins laid out under glass in a quiet room.
abstract.cn: 想象安静房间里玻璃下的钱币展品。

examples.en: She put the plates back in the cabinet.
examples.cn: 她把盘子放回橱柜。

examples.en: The cabinet met to discuss the budget.
examples.cn: 内阁开会讨论预算。

examples.en: The coin cabinet is upstairs.
examples.cn: 钱币陈列室在楼上。

dict_mnemonic.text: cabinet 和 cabin 同源，都是小空间；先记住小木屋，再想屋里靠墙立着带门的柜子，最后想到关起门议事的内阁。

root: cabinet 是古法语 cabine（小房间）的指小形式，本指私密小室，后来指室内的储物柜，又指在小室议事的政府顾问团。

sensesIntro.en: A storage cupboard, a group of senior ministers, and a display room.
sensesIntro.cn: 储物橱柜、高级部长组成的班子，以及陈列室。

branches.en: a medicine cabinet
branches.cn: 药柜

branches.en: a cabinet meeting
branches.cn: 内阁会议

branches.cn: 钱币陈列室

intro.cn: cabinet 能与 maker 组成复合词，也能加 -ry 构成名词。

latinIntro.en: The base is a French diminutive; the Latin relative is capanna, a hut.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是法语的指小形式，拉丁语中的相关词是 capanna（小屋）。

items.meaning: a small room, then a cupboard
a flat board for storing things

definition_zh: 一帮；团伙；结伙对付
definition_en: a group of people who are together, often for crime or work, or to unite against someone
core_image: 一群年轻人聚在街角低声说话
scene: 一帮年轻人站在街角。 A gang of young people stood on the corner.
sceneCN: 这里 gang 是「一帮」（第 1 个义项）；句意：一帮年轻人站在街角。

senses.title: A group together
senses.definition: a group of people who are together for a shared purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为共同目的聚在一起的一群人
senses.example: A gang of young people stood on the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 一帮年轻人站在街角。
senses.why: This is the neutral group sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是中性的群体义项。

senses.title: Criminal group
senses.definition: an organized group of criminals
senses.definitionCN: 有组织的犯罪集团
senses.example: Police broke up the gang last year.
senses.exampleCN: 警方去年打掉了这个团伙。
senses.why: The group sense darkened into crime.
senses.whyCN: 群体义项引申出犯罪团伙。

senses.definition: to join together to attack or oppose someone
senses.definitionCN: 联合起来攻击或反对某人
senses.example: The older boys ganged up on him.
senses.exampleCN: 大一点的男孩们联合起来对付他。
senses.why: The noun became a verb of uniting.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为表示联合的动词。

intro.en: Gang comes from an Old English verb meaning to go.
intro.cn: gang 来自古英语中意为「行走」的动词。

items.en: Gangan meant to go.
items.cn: gangan 意为行走。

items.en: A gang meant a going or a set.
items.cn: gang 指一次出行或一组人。

items.en: It named a group of workers.
items.cn: 它指一组工人。

items.en: It named a criminal group.
items.cn: 它指犯罪团伙。

items.en: Gang up on means unite against.
items.cn: gang up on 意为联合对付。

note.en: Gang is compared with look-alike words and words for groups.
note.cn: 把 gang 与形近词以及表示群体的词作比较。

entries.definition: to obtain
to suspend something
sounded a bell
a number of people together
a team that works together
a group with a shared activity

normalIntro.en: A gang is people moving together, for good work or for trouble.
normalIntro.cn: gang 是一起行动的人，可能为工作，也可能为祸。

normal.en: A gang of young people stood on the corner.
normal.cn: 一帮年轻人站在街角。

normal.en: Police broke up the gang last year.
normal.cn: 警方去年打掉了这个团伙。

normal.en: The older boys ganged up on him.
normal.cn: 大一点的男孩们联合起来对付他。

normal.en: A work gang repaired the road.
normal.cn: 一个工班修好了这条路。

normal.en: The gang members were arrested.
normal.cn: 团伙成员被逮捕了。

abstract.en: A crowd becomes a danger when it stops thinking as many.
abstract.cn: 当人群不再各自思考时，就会变成危险。

abstract.en: Belonging is a need that gangs misuse.
abstract.cn: 归属感是一种被团伙滥用的需求。

abstract.en: People who move together leave one track.
abstract.cn: 一起行动的人只留下一条足迹。

examples.en: A gang of young people stood on the corner.
examples.cn: 一帮年轻人站在街角。

examples.en: Police broke up the gang last year.
examples.cn: 警方去年打掉了这个团伙。

examples.en: A work gang repaired the road.
examples.cn: 一个工班修好了这条路。

dict_mnemonic.text: gang 与 gain、hang 形近；a gang of 是「一帮」，gang up on 是「联合起来对付」。

root: 由古英语 gangan（行走）演变而来，核心义「一起行动的一群人」。

sensesIntro.en: Gang is a group, a criminal group, or the act of uniting against someone.
sensesIntro.cn: gang 指一群人、犯罪团伙，或联合起来对付某人。

core.en: People moving as one group.
core.cn: 作为一个群体共同行动的人。

branches.en: Young people gather on a corner.
branches.cn: 年轻人聚在街角。

branches.en: Criminals organize as a group.
branches.cn: 罪犯组织成团伙。

branches.en: A group turns against one person.
branches.cn: 一群人转而对付一个人。

branches.en: Grouping and uniting are one process.
branches.cn: 成群与联合是同一个过程。

branches.en: Ganging up is the gang's method.
branches.cn: 结伙围攻是团伙的手法。

intro.en: Gang builds words for groups and passages.
intro.cn: gang 构成表示群体和通道的词。

latinIntro.en: Gang is a native English word, not Latin.
latinIntro.cn: gang 是英语本族词，不是拉丁语。

items.example: A gang met behind the hall.
items.exampleCN: 一帮人在礼堂后面碰头。

items.example: Rival gangs fought in the street.
items.exampleCN: 对立的团伙在街上打斗。

items.example: The boys ganged together against the rule.
items.exampleCN: 男孩们联合起来反对那条规则。

items.example: They were ganging up on the new student.
items.exampleCN: 他们正联合起来欺负新同学。

items.meaning: a leader of a work gang
items.example: The ganger gave the signal to start.

items.meaning: a member of a criminal gang
items.example: The gangster was caught at the port.
Do not gang up on one person.
items.exampleCN: 不要几个人一起对付一个人。

definition_zh: 描述；说明；种类
definition_en: words that tell what someone or something is like
core_image: 一张纸上密密麻麻写着细节，读到的人眼前慢慢浮出画面
scene: 招工启事上列着一长串要做的事，应聘者逐条对照自己会不会。 The job description lists every task in clear order.
sceneCN: 这里 description 指「说明文字」（第 2 个义项：逐条说明事物内容的文字）；句意是职位说明把每项任务按清楚的顺序列出。

senses.title: Words that paint a scene
senses.definition: a spoken or written account of what someone or something is like
senses.definitionCN: 口头或书面说出某人某物样子的叙述
senses.example: Her description of the village was full of small details.
senses.exampleCN: 她对那个村庄的描述满是细小的细节。
senses.why: A good account lets a stranger see a place he has never entered.
senses.whyCN: 好的叙述能让陌生人看见一个从未走进的地方。

senses.title: A written set of details
senses.definition: a piece of writing that explains what something is or how it works
senses.definitionCN: 解释某物是什么或如何运作的文字
senses.example: The job description lists every task in clear order.
senses.exampleCN: 职位说明把每项任务按清楚的顺序列出。
senses.why: Once the picture is fixed on paper, it can be checked and followed.
senses.whyCN: 画面一旦落到纸上，就能被核对、被照着做。

senses.title: A kind or type
senses.definition: a group of people or things of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 同一类的人或物
senses.example: They sell hats of every description in that shop.
senses.exampleCN: 那家店卖各式各样的帽子。
senses.why: When a kind has no name, people point to the picture it makes.
senses.whyCN: 一类东西没有名字时，人们就指着它呈现的样子来说。

intro.en: Description is the Latin noun descriptio, a drawing or a written copy, formed from de- and scribere, to write.
intro.cn: description 是拉丁名词 descriptio，意为图画或抄本，由 de- 与 scribere（写）构成。

items.en: Descriptio could mean a drawing, a copy or a written account.
items.cn: descriptio 可以指图画、抄本或书面叙述。

items.en: The city planner used it for laying out land on paper.
items.cn: 城市规划者用它来表示在纸上划分土地。

items.en: English borrowed it as the noun standing behind the verb describe.
items.cn: 英语把它借来，作为动词 describe 背后的名词。

items.en: It widened from pictures to any set of stated facts.
items.cn: 它从图画扩展到任何一组被陈述的事实。

items.en: It now even names a type, as in hats of every description.
items.cn: 如今它甚至用来指种类，如各式各样的帽子。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the script shape, and the meaning group moves from a spoken account to a rough drawing.
note.cn: 形近组共用 script 这一形状，近义组则从口头叙述一路走到粗略的草图。

entries.definition: to say what something is like
giving a picture in words
a doctor's written order for medicine
a report of an event
a written or spoken statement of facts
entries.definitionCN: 书面或口头的实情陈述

entries.definition: a short rough account or drawing

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a hand drawing shapes in the air and end with a list of details on paper.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一只手在空中画形状开始，落到纸上的一列细节。

normal.en: A description is a picture made of words instead of lines.
normal.cn: 一段描述就是用词而不是线条画出的图。

normal.en: If a listener can draw it, the description worked.
normal.cn: 如果听的人能画出来，这段描述就成立。

normal.en: De- plus scribere is writing something down from top to bottom.
normal.cn: de- 加 scribere，就是把东西从上到下写下来。

normal.en: A job description writes down what a job will ask of you.
normal.cn: 职位说明写下的，是这份工作会向你要什么。

normal.en: Of every description means the shelf holds all kinds.
normal.cn: of every description 就是说架子上什么种类都有。

abstract.en: Picture a finger tracing a face in the empty air.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指在空里描出一张脸。

abstract.en: Picture a list so exact that two strangers pick the same coat.
abstract.cn: 想象一份清单精确到两个陌生人会挑中同一件外套。

abstract.en: Picture a museum label longer than the thing it names.
abstract.cn: 想象一张比它所标注的展品还长的标签。

examples.en: The job description lists every task in clear order.
examples.cn: 职位说明把每项任务按清楚的顺序列出。

examples.en: She gave a detailed description of the missing bag.
examples.cn: 她详细描述了那个丢失的包。

examples.en: They sell hats of every description in that shop.
examples.cn: 那家店卖各式各样的帽子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 description 记成「地斯快普神」：de 向下，script 是写，把样子写下来，就成了描述与说明。

root: 来自拉丁语 descriptio，由 de-（向下）与 scribere（写）构成。本义是描画与抄写，指把事物的样子照样记下来；后来指口头的叙述、书面的说明，又引申为种类。

sensesIntro.en: From a picture built in words, to a written sheet of details, to a whole kind of thing.
sensesIntro.cn: 从用词搭起的画面，到写满细节的一张纸，再到一整类东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a written outline that lets a reader see the thing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份让读者看见实物的书面轮廓。

branches.en: The first sense is the scene rebuilt inside a listener.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是在听者心里重建起来的场景。

branches.en: The second sense is the same account fixed on paper for use.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是同一份叙述固定到纸上供人使用。

branches.en: The third sense stretches the word from one thing to a whole class.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把词从一件东西拉长到一整类。

branches.en: Spoken and written accounts differ only in where they are stored.
branches.cn: 口头与书面的叙述，差别只在于存放在哪里。

branches.en: A sheet that lists details can also stand for the type it describes.
branches.cn: 一张列出细节的纸，也能代表它所描述的那一类。

intro.en: Description is the noun at the centre of a family about writing things down.
intro.cn: description 是一族词的中心名词，这一族都关于把东西写下来。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is scribere, to write, with de- giving the sense of writing out in full.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 scribere（写），前缀 de- 给出「完整写出」的意思。

items.exampleCN: 这个描述与那个窃贼相符。
把那个房间描述给我听。
这是一个描述性的标题。
这个词是以描述方式使用的。

items.meaning: able to be put into words
items.exampleCN: 这种感觉几乎无法描述。

items.meaning: a word or sign that labels
items.example: Add a descriptor to each file.
items.exampleCN: 给每个文件加一个标识词。

items.example: He wore a nondescript grey coat.
items.exampleCN: 他穿着一件不起眼的灰色外套。

definition_zh: 分发；分布；配送
definition_en: the act of giving things out to many people, or the way things are spread over an area
core_image: 一张地图上散着许多小点，越靠中间越密
scene: 地图铺在桌上，小点东一堆西一堆。 The distribution of rainfall is uneven this year.
sceneCN: 这里 distribution 指「分布」（第 2 个义项：散在各处的状况）；句意是今年的降雨分布很不均匀。

senses.title: The act of giving out
senses.definition: the act of giving parts of something to many people
senses.definitionCN: 把东西一份份给许多人的行为
senses.example: The distribution of blankets began at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 分发毯子在中午开始。
senses.why: Fairness lives in the moment each share leaves the pile.
senses.whyCN: 公平就藏在每一份离开那堆东西的那一刻。

senses.title: The way things are spread
senses.definition: the pattern in which things are placed over an area
senses.definitionCN: 事物在一片地方上摆开的格局
senses.example: The map shows the distribution of rainfall.
senses.exampleCN: 这张图显示降雨的分布。
senses.why: A pattern is only visible when you step back from the dots.
senses.whyCN: 退后一步，才看得见许多点排成的样子。

senses.title: The business of delivering goods
senses.definition: the work of storing goods and sending them to shops
senses.definitionCN: 把货物存放并送到店铺的工作
senses.example: He works in distribution for a food company.
senses.exampleCN: 他在一家食品公司做配送。
senses.why: Someone must move the box from the factory to the shelf.
senses.whyCN: 总得有人把箱子从工厂搬到货架上。

intro.en: Distribution is Latin distributio, a dealing out, from distribuere, to assign in parts.
intro.cn: distribution 是拉丁语 distributio（分派），来自 distribuere（按份分给）。

items.en: Tribuere meant to grant a person a share.
items.cn: tribuere 指分给某人一份。

items.en: Dis- marked the splitting of one whole into parts.
items.cn: dis- 标出一个整体被分成几份。

items.en: Distributio named the settled pattern of shares.
items.cn: distributio 指分好之后形成的格局。

items.en: English used it for the sharing of goods.
items.cn: 英语借入时指物品的分配。

items.en: Trade gave it the sense of moving goods to shops.
items.cn: 商业让它有了把货运到店铺的意思。

items.en: Today it covers wealth, rainfall and parcel routes.
items.cn: 今天它可以指财富、降雨，也指包裹路线。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the tribute stem, while the meaning group names other patterns of sharing.
note.cn: 形近组共享 tribute 这段词干，近义组则是几种分配与铺开的名目。

entries.definition: to give out in shares
a firm that passes goods to shops
entries.definitionCN: 把货物转给店铺的经销商

entries.definition: concerned with sharing out
an amount set aside for a purpose
the reach of something over an area
the carrying of goods to a place

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with dots on a map and end with a van unloading boxes at a shop door.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从地图上的小点开始，落到一辆车在店门口卸货。

normal.en: Dis- plus tribute plus -ion: the sharing has become a pattern.
normal.cn: dis 加 tribute 再加 ion，分配成了一种格局。

normal.en: The distribution of seats favours the big cities.
normal.cn: 席位的分配偏向大城市。

normal.en: An even distribution of weight keeps the table steady.
normal.cn: 重量分布均匀，桌子才稳。

normal.en: The company rebuilt its distribution after the flood.
normal.cn: 洪水之后公司重建了配送网络。

normal.en: Income distribution is the subject of the whole report.
normal.cn: 整份报告讲的是收入分配。

abstract.en: Picture dots scattered on a map, thick in the middle.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上散着许多点，中间最密。

abstract.en: Picture one pile divided carefully into equal shares.
abstract.cn: 想象一堆东西被仔细分成相等的几份。

abstract.en: Picture a van leaving a warehouse before sunrise.
abstract.cn: 想象天没亮，一辆车开出仓库。

examples.en: The distribution of the prizes took only ten minutes.
examples.cn: 发奖只用了十分钟。

examples.en: The map shows the distribution of the species.
examples.cn: 这张图显示了该物种的分布。

examples.en: She found work in distribution after college.
examples.cn: 她大学毕业后在配送行业找到了工作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 distribution 记成「分开给开的样子」：dis 表示分开，tribute 表示给，加上名词尾，既指分发这件事，也指分完之后散开的格局。

root: 源自拉丁语 distributio，来自 distribuere（按份分给），由 dis-（分开）与 tribuere（分给）构成。本义是把一份份分出去，后来指分完之后呈现的格局，于是兼有「分配」与「分布」两义，现代又添了货物配送的意思。

sensesIntro.en: From shares leaving a pile to a pattern of dots that only appears when you step back.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一份份离开那堆东西，到退后一步才看得见的点点格局。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many small dots scattered on a map, thickest near the middle.
core.cn: 核心意象：地图上散着许多小点，越靠中间越密。

branches.en: The first sense is the act of handing out shares.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是把一份份发出去的动作。

branches.en: The second sense is the pattern those shares make.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是这些份数排出的格局。

branches.en: The third sense is the trade that moves goods to shops.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是把货运到店铺的行业。

branches.en: Both senses concern how a whole is divided.
branches.cn: 两个义项都关乎一个整体怎样被分开。

branches.en: Both senses can be shown on a map of routes.
branches.cn: 两个义项都能画在路线图上。

intro.en: Distribution sits in the tribuere family, where Latin tribuere, to assign, gives a whole set of sharing words.
intro.cn: distribution 属于 tribuere 一族，拉丁语 tribuere（分给）生出一整组表示分配的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin tribuere, to assign, gives tribute and contribute; the suffix -ion turns the act into a pattern.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tribuere（分给）给出 tribute 与 contribute，后缀 -ion 把动作变成一种格局。

items.meaning: the act or pattern of sharing out

items.exampleCN: 这家经销商覆盖三个省。

items.meaning: to give into a common pool

items.example: He attributes the delay to rain.
They paid tribute to the old coach.

definition_zh: 王冠；王位；顶部；为…加冕
definition_en: a circle worn on the head by a ruler, or the top part of something
core_image: 一顶镶着宝石的金冠稳稳压在王座上方那颗头上
scene: 加冕那天，金冠被缓缓放到新王头上。 The crown passed to his daughter.
sceneCN: 这里 crown 指「王冠」（第 1 个义项：君主戴在头上的环形饰物）；句意是王冠传给了他的女儿。

senses.title: A ruler's circle of gold
senses.definition: a circle of gold and jewels worn on the head by a ruler
senses.definitionCN: 君主戴在头上的金玉环形饰物
senses.example: The crown sat on a velvet cushion.
senses.exampleCN: 王冠放在一只天鹅绒垫子上。
senses.why: A circle on the head marks the one who stands above all.
senses.whyCN: 头顶一个圆环，标出那个高过所有人的人。

senses.title: Royal power itself
senses.definition: the power or position of a king or queen
senses.definitionCN: 国王或女王所拥有的权力或地位
senses.example: He gave up the crown for love.
senses.exampleCN: 他为了爱放弃了王位。
senses.why: The object stands for the office it marks.
senses.whyCN: 那件实物，代表了它所标记的那个位置。

senses.title: The highest part
senses.definition: the top or highest part of a head, a tree or a hill
senses.definitionCN: 头、树或山最高的那部分
senses.example: A bird sat on the crown of the tree.
senses.exampleCN: 一只鸟停在树顶。
senses.why: The top of anything wears a small crown of its own.
senses.whyCN: 任何东西的顶部，都自带一顶小冠。

intro.en: Crown comes from Latin corona, a wreath, through Old French corone.
intro.cn: crown 源自拉丁语 corona（花环），经古法语 corone 进入英语。

items.en: Corona meant a wreath or a circle.
items.cn: corona 指花环或圆环。

items.en: It was given to victors and to brides.
items.cn: 它被戴在胜利者与新娘头上。

items.en: Corone named a royal circlet.
items.cn: corone 指君王所戴的环形冠。

items.en: Crown named the king's circlet.
items.cn: crown 指国王的环形冠冕。

items.en: It came to mean royal power itself.
items.cn: 它开始指王权本身。

items.en: It also names the top of a head, a hill or a tooth.
items.cn: 它也指头、山或牙齿的顶部。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the crown spelling, and the meaning group names other seats or signs of royal power.
note.cn: 形近组共享 crown 这串拼写，近义组列出其他王权的象征与位置。

entries.definition: having a crown, or made king
entries.definitionCN: 戴着王冠的，或被立为王的

entries.definition: forming the finest final point
without a crown or a ruler
the seat and office of a ruler
a small crown worn by a noble
a ring of leaves or flowers

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a ring of gold and end with the top of an old tree.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一个金环开始，最后落到一棵老树的顶梢。

normal.en: Crown began as a wreath, and a wreath is a circle.
normal.cn: crown 本是花环，而花环就是一个圆。

normal.en: A circle has no beginning, which suits a king.
normal.cn: 圆没有起点，这正合一位君王。

normal.en: The crown is heavy because the office is.
normal.cn: 冠很重，因为那个位置很重。

normal.en: Every hill wears its own crown of trees.
normal.cn: 每一座山都戴着属于自己的树冠。

normal.en: To crown a day is to give it a perfect end.
normal.cn: 为一天加冕，就是给它一个完美的结尾。

abstract.en: Picture gold resting on red velvet.
abstract.cn: 想象金子搁在红色天鹅绒上。

abstract.en: Picture a head bowed to receive a ring.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗低下去接住圆环的头。

abstract.en: Picture a single tree above the whole forest.
abstract.cn: 想象整片林子之上的一棵树。

examples.en: The crown was kept in a locked room.
examples.cn: 王冠被锁在一间屋子里。

examples.en: She succeeded to the crown at twenty.
examples.cn: 她二十岁继承王位。

examples.en: Snow crowned the top of the mountain.
examples.cn: 雪覆盖了山顶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 crown 记成头顶上那个金环：戴上它是王冠，戴在山上就是山顶。

root: 源自拉丁语 corona（花环、圆环），经古法语 corone 进入英语；本义是戴在头上的环，后指王冠与王权，再引申为任何事物的顶部。

sensesIntro.en: From a circle on a head, to the power it stands for, to the top of anything at all.
sensesIntro.cn: 从头上的一只圆环，到它所代表的权力，再到任何事物的顶端。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gold ring resting on a bowed head.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只金环落在低下的头顶。

branches.en: The ring itself is the first meaning.
branches.cn: 那只圆环本身，是最早的意思。

branches.en: The object then stands for the power behind it.
branches.cn: 这件实物随后代表了它背后的权力。

branches.en: Any highest point is crowned by its own top.
branches.cn: 任何最高处，都被自己的顶端加冕。

branches.en: Gold and authority are worn together.
branches.cn: 金子和权威，被一起戴在头上。

branches.en: A king and a hill both carry a crown.
branches.cn: 国王和山丘，都顶着一顶冠。

intro.en: Crown is a short word that builds crowned, crowning and uncrowned.
intro.cn: crown 是个短词，能组成 crowned、crowning 与 uncrowned。

latinIntro.en: The Latin corona, a wreath, is the source of crown and of coronation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 corona（花环）是 crown 与 coronation 的源头。

items.meaning: a ring worn by a ruler
items.example: The crown shone under the lamp.
Two crowns were kept in the vault.
The king was crowned at dawn.

items.exampleCN: 最辉煌的一刻出现在最后。

items.example: The crownless prince left the hall.
items.exampleCN: 未戴冠的王子离开了大厅。

items.example: The coronation drew a huge crowd.

items.meaning: a small crown of a noble
items.example: A thin coronet held her hair.
items.exampleCN: 一顶细小的冠束住她的头发。

latinEntries.example: Latin corona first named a wreath.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 corona 最初指花环。

definition_zh: 撕；扯破；裂口；敲竹杠
definition_en: to tear something quickly, or a torn place
core_image: 被撕成两半的信封
scene: 她不小心把信封撕成了两半。 She accidentally ripped the envelope in half.
sceneCN: 这里 rip 是「撕」（第 1 个义项：用力快速把东西扯开）；句意：她不小心把信封撕成了两半。

senses.title: Tearing quickly
senses.definition: to tear something with force
senses.definitionCN: 用力把某物撕开
senses.example: He ripped the letter into small pieces.
senses.exampleCN: 他把信撕成了小片。
senses.why: Rip suggests a fast, rough pull.
senses.whyCN: rip 意味着一记快速粗暴的拉扯。

senses.title: Charging too much
senses.definition: to charge an unfair price
senses.definitionCN: 收取不公平的价格
senses.example: That shop rips off tourists.
senses.exampleCN: 那家店宰游客。
senses.why: Ripping away money feels like tearing cloth.
senses.whyCN: 把钱撕走就像撕布一样。

senses.title: A torn place
senses.definition: a hole or tear in something
senses.definitionCN: 物体上的破洞或裂口
senses.example: There is a rip in my coat.
senses.exampleCN: 我的外套上有个裂口。
senses.why: The noun keeps the shape of the tear.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了撕裂的形状。

intro.en: Rip is a Middle English word, probably from a Scandinavian source, meaning to tear.
intro.cn: rip 是中古英语词，可能来自斯堪的纳维亚语，意为撕开。

items.en: Rippen means to tear.
items.cn: rippen 意为撕。

items.en: A related northern word also means to tear.
items.cn: 北欧的相关词同样意为撕。

items.en: Rip becomes common for cloth and paper.
items.cn: rip 常用于布料和纸张。

items.en: Rip off grows into a slang phrase.
items.cn: rip off 发展为俚语短语。

items.en: The noun names a tear in fabric.
items.cn: 名词指织物上的撕口。

note.en: Rip is a fast, rough tear; tear itself is the general word.
note.cn: rip 是快速粗暴的撕，tear 是一般的撕裂。

entries.definition: ready to be eaten
torn or very fit
a small wave
to pull something apart
to tear into thin strips
to make a long narrow cut

normalIntro.en: Rip is the sound and speed of a tear.
normalIntro.cn: rip 就是撕裂的声音与速度。

normal.en: Rip open means tear it at once.
normal.cn: rip open 意为立刻撕开。

normal.en: Rip apart means tear it into pieces.
normal.cn: rip apart 意为撕成碎片。

normal.en: Rip off means charge far too much.
normal.cn: rip off 意为要价过高。

normal.en: A rip in the paper is a torn place.
normal.cn: a rip in the paper 是一处撕口。

normal.en: Ripped jeans are torn on purpose.
normal.cn: ripped jeans 是故意撕破的牛仔裤。

abstract.en: Picture cloth parting with a sharp sound.
abstract.cn: 想象布料伴着锐响裂开。

abstract.en: Imagine a page pulled in two by quick hands.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手飞快地把纸页扯成两半。

abstract.en: Think of a lightning tear across the sky.
abstract.cn: 想象闪电在天空撕开一道口子。

examples.en: The dog ripped my new shirt.
examples.cn: 狗撕破了我新买的衬衫。

examples.en: Do not rip off the label yet.
examples.cn: 先别把标签撕掉。

examples.en: There was a long rip in the tent.
examples.cn: 帐篷上有一道长长的裂口。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rip」听起来像「裂扑」——一下裂开扑啦响，就是撕。

root: 中古英语 rippen（撕）→ rip，核心义「快速粗暴地扯开」；俚语义「敲竹杠」像把钱撕走。

sensesIntro.en: Rip means to tear something quickly, to overcharge, or a torn place.
sensesIntro.cn: rip 意为快速撕开、敲竹杠，或指一处裂口。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: cloth parting with a sharp sound.
core.cn: 核心意象：布料伴着锐响裂开。

branches.en: The fast pull is the core action.
branches.cn: 快速拉扯是核心动作。

branches.en: Pulling away money becomes overcharging.
branches.cn: 把钱拉走引申为敲竹杠。

branches.en: The noun keeps the shape of the tear.
branches.cn: 名词保留了撕口的形状。

branches.en: The action and its result share one image.
branches.cn: 动作与结果共享同一个意象。

branches.en: Both cloth and wallets can be ripped.
branches.cn: 布料与钱包都可能被「撕」。

intro.en: Rip is a short native verb with no prefix.
intro.cn: rip 是简短的本族动词，没有前缀。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic rather than Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属于日耳曼语而非拉丁语。

items.exampleCN: 破洞牛仔裤是一种风格。

items.example: The phrase adds a slang sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语增加了俚语义。
这个短语体现快速动作。

definition_zh: 破坏；糟蹋；宠坏；变质；（名）战利品；赃物
definition_en: to harm or ruin something, or goods taken by force in war
core_image: 一颗好苹果在篮子里慢慢烂开，褐斑一圈圈扩大
scene: 野餐垫上摆着装水果的篮子。 The hot sun spoiled the fruit before lunch even started.
sceneCN: 这里 spoil 是「使变质、毁坏」（第 1 个义项：损坏食物或事物）；句意为烈日在午餐开始前就把水果晒坏了。图中可辨识物件：野餐垫、水果篮、日光。

pos.zh: 动词：破坏；糟蹋；宠坏；变质

collocations.phrase: spare the rod and spoil the child

derivatives.zh: 英式过去分词作形容词，义为「被宠坏的；变质的」
由动词加施动后缀构成，义为「剧透；破坏者」
由 de- 加本词构成，义为「掠夺；蹂躏」（书面）

senses.title: To ruin or damage something
senses.definition: to harm or reduce the value or quality of something
senses.definitionCN: 损害或降低某物的价值与品质
senses.example: One loud engine spoiled the quiet of the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 一声轰鸣的发动机毁掉了山谷的宁静。
senses.why: The good thing rots from the point where force or neglect touches it.
senses.whyCN: 好物从强力或疏忽触碰之点开始腐烂。

senses.title: To make food unfit to eat
senses.definition: to make food or perishable goods go bad
senses.definitionCN: 使食物或易腐物品变坏
senses.example: The milk spoiled overnight in the warm kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 牛奶在温暖的厨房里一夜之间变质了。
senses.why: What was stored for later is taken by decay now.
senses.whyCN: 为以后存的口粮，此刻被腐坏夺走。

senses.title: To treat a child too indulgently
senses.definition: to give a child too much of what it wants, so it behaves badly
senses.definitionCN: 对孩子有求必应，致其任性
senses.example: Grandparents spoiled the twins with sweets and late nights.
senses.exampleCN: 祖父母用糖果和熬夜把双胞胎宠坏了。
senses.why: Too much sweetness is itself a kind of ruin.
senses.whyCN: 过多的甜本身就是一种毁坏。

senses.title: To rob or plunder
senses.definition: to take goods by force, in older usage
senses.definitionCN: 以强力夺取财物，旧用法
senses.example: The raiders spoiled the granaries of the village.
senses.exampleCN: 劫掠者抢走了村庄的谷仓。
senses.why: Before the ruin sense, the taking of goods was the core.
senses.whyCN: 在毁坏义之前，夺取财物才是核心。

senses.title: Spoils: goods taken in war
senses.definition: goods or property seized by the victors in a war
senses.definitionCN: 战争胜利者夺取的财物
senses.example: The victors divided the spoils of the captured city.
senses.exampleCN: 胜利者瓜分了攻陷城池的战利品。
senses.why: What war ruins on one side becomes gain on the other.
senses.whyCN: 战争毁掉一方的，成了另一方的所得。

senses.title: Spoils: profits of an enterprise
senses.definition: benefits or profits gained from an activity, as in share the spoils
senses.definitionCN: 从活动中获得的好处，如分赃之说
senses.example: The two firms agreed to share the spoils of the new market.
senses.exampleCN: 两家公司约定瓜分新市场的收益。
senses.why: Plunder grows a business suit: gain taken from a contest.
senses.whyCN: 掠夺换上西装：从竞争中夺取的收益。

senses.title: To weaken a vote by marking it wrongly
senses.definition: to mark a ballot wrongly so that it cannot be counted
senses.definitionCN: 在选票上误填使其无法计入
senses.example: He spoiled his ballot by writing on it twice.
senses.exampleCN: 他在选票上写了两处，使其作废。
senses.why: A ruined paper ruins the choice it carried.
senses.whyCN: 被毁的纸毁掉了它所承载的选择。

senses.title: To spoil for: to eager for a fight
senses.definition: to have a strong desire for a fight or contest
senses.definitionCN: 极欲争斗或较量
senses.example: The young player was spoiling for a rematch.
senses.exampleCN: 年轻球员憋着一股劲要重赛一场。
senses.why: The ruined mood turns restless, hunting for an outlet.
senses.whyCN: 被搅坏的心气不得安宁，四处寻衅。

intro.en: Spoil is a Latin plunder-word that drifted from taking goods to ruining them.
intro.cn: spoil 是拉丁语的掠夺词，从夺取财物漂移为毁坏财物。

items.en: *spel- is generally reconstructed as "to split off, break off"; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *spel- 表示「剥落、掰下」；更早来源不确定。

items.en: Latin spoliare meant "to strip of skin or goods, to plunder", from spolium "skin, hide taken from prey".
items.cn: 拉丁语 spoliare 意为「剥取皮毛、掠夺」，出自 spolium「猎物之皮」。

items.en: Late Latin spoiliare passed into Old French espoillier with the plundering sense.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 spoiliare 经古法语 espoillier 保留掠夺义。

items.en: English took the word in the fourteenth century as a verb of plunder.
items.cn: 英语于十四世纪收下该词，作掠夺动词。

items.en: The sense shifted to ruining and spoiling, while spoils kept the plunder meaning.
items.cn: 词义转向毁坏与糟蹋，而 spoils 保留掠夺义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the plunder family and near spellings; the near-meaning group gathers words of ruining and loot.
note.cn: 形近组收掠夺词族与拼写相近的词；近义组收表示毁坏与赃物的词。

entries.definition: British past form, also an adjective for pampered children.
entries.definitionCN: 英式过去式，也作形容词形容被宠坏的孩子。

entries.definition: A formal verb meaning to strip a place of its wealth.
entries.definitionCN: 正式动词，义为「掠夺一地之财」。

entries.definition: A legal term for the destruction or plundering of property.
entries.definitionCN: 法律术语，指财产的毁损或掠夺。

entries.definition: Earth or to stain; one letter apart and of different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「土壤；弄脏」；仅一字母之差，词源不同。

entries.definition: Something that spoils, or a plot detail given away.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指破坏者或被剧透的情节。

entries.definition: To destroy completely, stronger and more final than spoil.
entries.definitionCN: 彻底摧毁，比 spoil 更强、更不可逆。

entries.definition: To smash and destroy, often of physical things.
To take goods by force, matching the old spoils sense.
entries.definitionCN: 以强力夺取财物，对应 spoils 旧义。

entries.definition: To impair the perfection of something, lighter than ruin.
entries.definitionCN: 损害某物的完美，程度轻于 ruin。

entries.definition: To indulge someone, matching the spoilt-child sense.

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the apple image and the plunder history the word really has.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用烂苹果意象，以及该词真实的掠夺史。

normal.en: Latin spolium was the skin stripped from prey: taking came first.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 spolium 是从猎物剥下的皮：先有夺取。

normal.en: The spoils of war are what the victors take home.
normal.cn: spoils of war 是胜利者带回家的东西。

normal.en: Spoilt food and spoilt children both got too much of something.
normal.cn: 变质的食物与被宠坏的孩子，都是「得了太多」。

normal.en: Spoiled with an -ed is American; spoilt with a -t is British.
normal.cn: -ed 的 spoiled 是美式，-t 的 spoilt 是英式。

normal.en: Spoiler alert: the warning that a plot will be spoiled.
normal.cn: spoiler alert：提醒剧情即将被「剧透」毁掉。

abstract.en: Brown spots spread one ring at a time: ruin rarely happens all at once.
abstract.cn: 褐斑一圈圈扩大：毁坏很少一瞬完成。

abstract.en: Too much sugar keeps the apple sweet and rots it early.
abstract.cn: 过多的糖让苹果保持甜，也提前把它催烂。

abstract.en: The basket is a small kingdom: whatever the strong take from it, the rest spoils.
abstract.cn: 篮子是个小王国：强者取走多少，剩下的就烂多少。

examples.en: Heavy rain spoiled the whole afternoon at the beach.
examples.cn: 大雨毁掉了海滩上整整一个下午。

examples.en: The meat will spoil if the fridge stops running.
examples.cn: 冰箱一停，肉就会变质。

examples.en: Winners once divided the spoils openly among the crew.
examples.cn: 从前胜利者会在船员间公开分赃。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯波伊尔」——好苹果一圈圈烂开：毁坏；战利品

root: spoil 经古法语 espoillier「掠夺」追溯至拉丁语 spoliare「剥取、劫掠」，出自 spolium「猎物之皮」；一般认为印欧词根 *spel- 表示「剥落」，更早来源不确定。despoil、spoliation 同族。

sensesIntro.en: The senses of spoil move from taking to ruining: plunder first, then decay, indulgence, and the profits of a contest.
sensesIntro.cn: spoil 的义项从夺取走向毁坏：先是掠夺，继而是腐坏、溺爱与竞争所得。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a good apple spreading brown rings inside the basket.
core.cn: 核心意象：篮中一颗好苹果，褐斑一圈圈扩散。

branches.en: THE ROT LINE: neglect, warmth or too much sweetness ruins the good thing.
branches.cn: 腐烂线：疏忽、温热或过量甜分毁掉好物。

branches.en: THE PLUNDER LINE: the oldest sense takes goods by force.
branches.cn: 掠夺线：最古老的义以强力夺财。

branches.en: THE BUSINESS LINE: contest profits wear the old plunder word.
branches.cn: 商业线：竞争所得披着旧的掠夺词。

branches.en: THE BALLOT LINE: one ruined paper ruins one vote.
branches.cn: 选票线：一张废纸毁掉一票。

branches.en: THE FIGHT LINE: a spoilt mood hunts for a contest.
branches.cn: 寻衅线：被搅坏的心气渴望较量。

intro.en: Spoil keeps its Latin plunder stem visible, and English adds simple endings.
intro.cn: spoil 的拉丁掠夺词干清晰可见；英语只加简单词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin spoliare and Old French espoillier are recorded; the Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 spoliare 与古法语 espoillier 均有记录，印欧词根为重构形式。

items.example: The noun is the seed of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是词族的种子。

items.example: The verb passed into French and English.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词进入法语与英语。

items.example: It carried the word into English.

items.exampleCN: 英式英语用 -t 构成 spoilt。

items.example: It keeps the Latin shape intact.
The plural keeps the plunder sense.

derivatives.zh: 英式过去分词作形容词，义为「被宠坏的；变质的」
由动词加施动后缀构成，义为「剧透；破坏者」
