definition_zh: 考虑；需要考虑的因素；体谅
definition_en: the act of thinking carefully about something, or a fact that must be weighed
core_image: 桌上摊着几张纸，一个人托着下巴逐条权衡
scene: 面试前夜，她把每个条件在纸上排了一遍。 After long consideration, she accepted the offer.
sceneCN: 这里 consideration 指「仔细考虑」（第 1 个义项：对某事反复权衡）；句意是经过长时间的考虑，她接受了这份工作。

pos.zh: 考虑；需要考虑的因素；体谅

senses.title: Careful thought
senses.definition: the act of thinking about something carefully before acting
senses.definitionCN: 行动之前对某事反复思考
senses.example: After much consideration, they chose the cheaper plan.
senses.exampleCN: 经过再三考虑，他们选择了更便宜的那个方案。
senses.why: A decision made in a hurry often misses what a slow look would catch.
senses.whyCN: 匆忙作出的决定，常常漏掉慢看时能看见的东西。

senses.title: A fact to weigh
senses.definition: something that must be taken into account when deciding
senses.definitionCN: 做决定时必须纳入权衡的事情
senses.example: Cost is only one consideration here.
senses.exampleCN: 在这里，成本只是需要考虑的一个因素。
senses.why: A good choice needs more than one item on the scale.
senses.whyCN: 好的选择需要天平上不只放一样东西。

senses.title: Thought for others
senses.definition: kind attention to the feelings of other people
senses.definitionCN: 对他人感受的体贴照顾
senses.example: He showed no consideration for the tired staff.
senses.exampleCN: 他对疲惫的员工毫不体谅。
senses.why: The same mind that weighs facts can also weigh feelings.
senses.whyCN: 权衡事实的那颗心，也能权衡别人的感受。

intro.en: Consideration comes from Latin considerare, to look at closely, a word once linked to sidus, a star, as if reading the sky.
intro.cn: consideration 来自拉丁语 considerare，意为仔细察看，旧说与 sidus（星星）有关，仿佛观星以定吉凶。

items.en: Sidus meant star, and considerare may once have meant to observe the stars.
items.cn: sidus 意为星星，considerare 最初可能指观察星象。

items.en: Considerare widened to mean examining anything with care.
items.cn: considerare 的词义扩大为仔细察看任何事物。

items.en: The noun consideratio named the act of careful looking.
items.cn: 名词 consideratio 指仔细察看这一行为。

items.en: French consideration carried the sense of respectful regard.
items.cn: 法语 consideration 带有尊重与顾念的含义。

items.en: English consideration first meant careful thought before a choice.
items.cn: 英语 consideration 最初指做选择前的仔细思考。

items.en: It now also names a single fact that must be weighed.
items.cn: 如今它也指必须纳入权衡的某一因素。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words from the same consider- family, and the meaning group names other kinds of careful thought.
note.cn: 形近组收的是同一个 consider- 词族的词，近义组列出其他表示仔细思量的说法。

entries.definition: thinking about the feelings of other people
large enough to be important
used to say that something is true when you think of the facts
the activity of thinking, or an idea produced by it
long and careful discussion before a decision
attention or care given to someone

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a slow look at the facts, then move to the single fact that tips a choice and to care for other people.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从慢慢端详事实开始，再到压动选择的那一个因素，最后落到对他人的体谅。

normal.en: Con- is together and sider is star, so consideration is reading the sky before you move.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，sider 是星星，consideration 就是先看星象再行动。

normal.en: A table with three papers on it: that is consideration at work.
normal.cn: 桌上摊着三张纸，这就是考虑正在进行的样子。

normal.en: One factor is not a decision, so consideration puts several on the scale.
normal.cn: 一个因素不成决定，所以考虑要把好几样放上天平。

normal.en: Consideration for others is the same word turned toward feelings.
normal.cn: 体谅不过是同一个词转向了感受这一边。

normal.en: Look twice, then act once.
normal.cn: 看两遍，再动手一次。

abstract.en: Picture a hand holding a scale that is still moving.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手扶着一架仍在晃动的天平。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp over a page full of small notes.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯照着一页密密麻麻的小字。

abstract.en: Picture a chair pulled out for someone who looks tired.
abstract.cn: 想象有人为一位显出疲态的人拉开椅子。

examples.en: After much consideration, she turned down the offer.
examples.cn: 经过反复考虑，她拒绝了那份邀约。

examples.en: Safety must be the first consideration in this design.
examples.cn: 在这个设计里，安全必须是首要的考虑。

examples.en: He treats his staff with real consideration.
examples.cn: 他对员工十分体谅。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 consideration 记成 con（一起）加 sider（星星）加 ation：像古人一起看星推演吉凶那样反复权衡，就是考虑。

root: 源自拉丁语 considerare（仔细察看），旧说与 sidus（星星）有关，仿佛观星以定吉凶，后指考虑、需要权衡的因素与体谅。

sensesIntro.en: From slow looking, to the facts that demand a look, and finally to looking after other people.
sensesIntro.cn: 从慢慢察看，到必须察看的事实，最后到照看别人的感受。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scale on a table with papers on both sides.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上放着一架天平，两边都压着纸。

branches.en: Careful thought slows the hand before it moves.
branches.cn: 仔细考虑让手在行动之前先慢下来。

branches.en: A single consideration can change the whole balance.
branches.cn: 一个因素就能改变整个平衡。

branches.en: The same habit of mind turns into kindness toward people.
branches.cn: 同一种思维习惯转向人，就成了体贴。

branches.en: Both senses put something on a scale and wait for it to settle.
branches.cn: 两个义项都是把东西放上天平，等它稳定下来。

branches.en: A person can be the factor that a careful mind weighs.
branches.cn: 人本身也可以成为那颗细心的心所权衡的因素。

intro.en: Consideration is built on Latin con-, together, plus considerare, to examine.
intro.cn: consideration 由拉丁语 con-（一起）与 considerare（察看）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin star base sider- also appears in sidereal, while the consider- family runs through consider and considerable.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的星词基 sider- 也出现在 sidereal 中，而 consider- 词族贯穿 consider 与 considerable。

items.meaning: the act of weighing something in the mind
items.meaningCN: 在心里权衡某事的行为
items.exampleCN: 这个计划正在考虑之中。

items.meaning: to examine something in the mind
worth noticing because of its size
items.example: The repair cost a considerable sum.
items.exampleCN: 这次修理花了一笔不小的钱。

items.example: It was considerate of you to call.

items.meaning: in a way that shows care for others
items.example: She spoke considerately to the child.
Loud music at midnight is inconsiderate.
items.exampleCN: 半夜大声放音乐是不替别人着想。

items.meaning: when you take the facts into account
items.example: She did well, considering her age.
items.exampleCN: 考虑到她的年龄，她做得很好。

items.meaning: to think about a choice once more

definition_zh: 竞争的；有竞争力的；争强好胜的
definition_en: relating to competition, cheap enough to beat rivals, or wanting very much to win
core_image: 跑道上的人侧头盯着旁边的选手，脚下加快
scene: 招聘会上，同一个岗位前排了很长的队。 The job market is highly competitive this year.
sceneCN: 这里 competitive 指「竞争激烈的」（第 1 个义项：充满竞争的）；句意是今年的就业市场竞争十分激烈。

pos.zh: 竞争的；有竞争力的；争强好胜的

senses.title: Full of competition
senses.definition: involving people or firms trying to win
senses.definitionCN: 涉及人或公司争胜的
senses.example: The software market is fiercely competitive.
senses.exampleCN: 软件市场竞争激烈。
senses.why: An adjective from competition simply describes the arena where rivals meet.
senses.whyCN: 由 competition 来的形容词，只描述对手相遇的场地。

senses.title: Good enough to win
senses.definition: low or good enough to beat what rivals offer
senses.definitionCN: 低或好到能胜过对手的
senses.example: They offered a competitive price on the laptop.
senses.exampleCN: 他们给这台笔记本报了个有竞争力的价格。
senses.why: From describing the contest, the word moves to describing a winning position in it.
senses.whyCN: 从描述比赛，转为描述在比赛中占优的位置。

senses.title: Eager to win
senses.definition: wanting very much to beat others
senses.definitionCN: 非常想胜过别人的
senses.example: He is too competitive to enjoy a friendly game.
senses.exampleCN: 他太争强好胜，玩不成轻松的游戏。
senses.why: The same drive can be praised in a market and frowned on at a dinner table.
senses.whyCN: 同一种冲劲在市场里被称赞，在饭桌上却被皱眉。

intro.en: Competitive adds the ending -ive to the Latin base of compete, naming what belongs to rivalry.
intro.cn: competitive 在 compete 的拉丁词基上加后缀 -ive，表示属于争胜的东西。

items.en: Competere meant to seek the same thing as another.
items.cn: competere 意为与别人追求同一样东西。

items.en: Competitivus described things that belonged to a contest.
items.cn: competitivus 描述属于争胜的事物。

items.en: English competitive first described sports and exams.
items.cn: 英语 competitive 最初描述体育与考试。

items.en: Trade writers applied it to prices and markets.
items.cn: 商业作者把它用到价格与市场上。

items.en: It now also describes a person who hates to lose.
items.cn: 如今它也用来形容输不起的人。

note.en: The look-alike group holds other compete forms, and the meaning group separates ambitious drive from an aggressive manner and a cheap price.
note.cn: 形近组收的是 compete 的其他形式，近义组分辨雄心、强势作风与低廉价格。

entries.definition: to strive against others
having enough skill for a task
a contest or a rivalry
determined to succeed
very forceful in pursuing a goal
low in price

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a sideways glance at a rival, then move to a price that wins and to a temper that must win.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从斜眼看向对手开始，再走到能取胜的价格与非赢不可的性子。

normal.en: Competitive carries -ive, so it describes a field full of competing.
normal.cn: competitive 带着 -ive，所以它描述一个充满竞争的场域。

normal.en: A competitive price is a price that competes and wins.
normal.cn: 有竞争力的价格，就是能参与竞争并胜出的价格。

normal.en: A competitive person keeps score even in the garden.
normal.cn: 好胜的人连在花园里也要计分。

normal.en: Competitive is the adjective, competitiveness the quality.
normal.cn: competitive 是形容词，competitiveness 是那种性质。

normal.en: The phrase competitive edge is the small gap that wins.
normal.cn: competitive edge 就是决定胜负的那一点点差距。

abstract.en: Picture a runner half a step ahead, breathing hard.
abstract.cn: 想象跑者领先半步，喘着粗气。

abstract.en: Picture two price tags, one lower by a few coins.
abstract.cn: 想象两个价签，一个低了几枚硬币。

abstract.en: Picture a chess player refusing a draw.
abstract.cn: 想象棋手拒绝和棋。

examples.en: Small shops struggle to stay competitive.
examples.cn: 小店很难保持竞争力。

examples.en: She has a competitive streak that shows in every game.
examples.cn: 她有一股好胜劲，每场游戏都看得出来。

examples.en: The hotel offers competitive rates in winter.
examples.cn: 这家酒店冬季价格很有竞争力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 competitive 记成 compete（竞争）加 itive：带着竞争劲儿的，就是有竞争力的、好胜的。

root: 源自拉丁语 competere（一起追求），加形容词后缀 -ive，本义属于竞争的，后引申为有竞争力的与争强好胜的。

sensesIntro.en: From the arena itself, to a winning price, and finally to the temper that must win.
sensesIntro.cn: 从场地本身，到能取胜的价格，最后到非赢不可的性子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a runner glancing sideways at a rival, feet quickening.
core.cn: 核心意象：跑道上的人侧头盯着旁边的选手，脚下加快。

branches.en: The first sense simply describes a crowded field.
branches.cn: 第一个义项只是描述一个人挤人的场域。

branches.en: A price earns the word when it can beat the shop next door.
branches.cn: 价格能压过隔壁店时，才配得上这个词。

branches.en: The same drive turns inward and becomes a temperament.
branches.cn: 同一种冲劲转向内里，就成了一种性情。

branches.en: A market is competitive because its offers compete.
branches.cn: 市场之所以叫竞争性，是因为其中的报价在相互竞争。

branches.en: Winning prices and winning tempers share one source.
branches.cn: 取胜的价格与好胜的性子同出一源。

intro.en: Competitive takes the Latin base compet- and the adjective ending -itive.
intro.cn: competitive 由拉丁词基 compet- 加形容词后缀 -itive 构成。

latinIntro.en: Every form in this family carries the seeking base pet-.
latinIntro.cn: 这一族的每个形式都带着表示追求的 pet- 词基。

items.meaning: in a way that competes well
items.exampleCN: 这个团队的报价很有竞争力。
这份报告给各国竞争力排名。
每位参赛者都领到一个徽章。

items.example: Two competitors withdrew at the start.
They compete on service, not price.
items.exampleCN: 他们比的是服务而不是价格。
相互竞争的说法让买家糊涂了。

definition_zh: 极端的；极度的；极端
definition_en: very great in degree; far from what is usual or moderate; the furthest point
core_image: 温度计的水银柱冲到最顶端
scene: 该地区正经历极端天气。 The region is experiencing extreme weather.
sceneCN: 这里 extreme 是「极度的、极端的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：该地区正经历极端天气。

senses.title: Very great in degree
senses.definition: very great in degree or intensity
senses.definitionCN: 程度或强度非常大的
senses.example: The desert reaches extreme temperatures.
senses.exampleCN: 沙漠会达到极端温度。
senses.why: The core sense is the farthest point of a scale.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是刻度上最远的一点。

senses.title: Far from moderate
senses.definition: far from what is usual, moderate, or acceptable
senses.definitionCN: 远离通常、温和或可接受范围的
senses.example: The group holds extreme views.
senses.exampleCN: 这个团体持有极端观点。
senses.why: The far end of a scale becomes a political judgment.
senses.whyCN: 刻度的远端变成政治判断。

senses.title: The furthest point
senses.definition: the furthest or most severe point of something
senses.definitionCN: 某事物最远或最严重的点
senses.example: The two extremes rarely meet.
senses.exampleCN: 两个极端很少相遇。
senses.why: The adjective becomes the endpoint itself.
senses.whyCN: 形容词变成端点本身。

intro.en: Extreme comes from Latin extremus, the superlative of exterus, outward.
intro.cn: extreme 来自拉丁语 extremus，是 exterus（向外的）的最高级。

items.en: Exterus means outward.
items.cn: exterus 意为向外的。

items.en: Extremus means farthest out.
items.cn: extremus 意为最靠外的。

items.en: Extreme passes through French into English.
items.cn: extreme 经法语进入英语。

items.en: Extreme describes the far end of a scale.
items.cn: extreme 描述刻度的最远端。

items.en: Extreme also describes severe weather and views.
items.cn: 现代英语中 extreme 也形容极端天气与观点。

note.en: Extreme is the far end; extra is an addition.
note.cn: extreme 是最远端，extra 则是额外添加。

entries.definition: to remove or take out
a person with special knowledge
to pass waste out of the body
very bad or intense
very strong or extreme
far beyond the usual

normalIntro.en: Extreme points to the farthest end of any scale.
normalIntro.cn: extreme 指向任何刻度的最远端。

normal.en: The region suffers extreme heat in summer.
normal.cn: 这个地区夏天酷热难耐。

normal.en: They took extreme measures to stop the fire.
normal.cn: 他们采取极端措施阻止大火。

normal.en: The family lives in extreme poverty.
normal.cn: 这家人生活在极度贫困中。

normal.en: Do not go to extremes in dieting.
normal.cn: 节食不要走极端。

normal.en: At the other extreme, the lake is frozen.
normal.cn: 在另一个极端，湖面结着冰。

abstract.en: Picture a thermometer pushed to its highest mark.
abstract.cn: 想象温度计的水银冲到最高点。

abstract.en: Imagine a road ending at a cliff edge.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路终止在悬崖边。

abstract.en: Think of a scale with weights at both ends.
abstract.cn: 想象天平两端都压着砝码。

examples.en: The mountain is dangerous in extreme weather.
examples.cn: 在极端天气下，这座山很危险。

examples.en: Their views are too extreme for most voters.
examples.cn: 他们的观点对多数选民来说太极端。

examples.en: The temperature swung from one extreme to the other.
examples.cn: 温度从一个极端摆到另一个极端。

dict_mnemonic.text: extreme 与 extra 同源：extra 是「超出」，extreme 是「超出到最远端」，即极端。

root: 源自拉丁语 extremus（最靠外的），是 exterus（向外的）的最高级，核心义「刻度或范围的最远端」。

sensesIntro.en: Extreme means very great in degree, far from moderate, or the furthest point.
sensesIntro.cn: extreme 意为程度极大、远离温和，或最远的端点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gauge needle at the red end.
core.cn: 核心意象：仪表指针停在红色末端。

branches.en: The base sense is the far end of a scale.
branches.cn: 基础义是刻度的最远端。

branches.en: The far end becomes a judgment of views.
branches.cn: 最远端变成对观点的评判。

branches.en: The adjective becomes the endpoint itself.
branches.cn: 形容词变成端点本身。

branches.en: Great degree and immoderate views both sit at the edge.
branches.cn: 极大程度与偏激观点都位于边缘。

branches.en: Extreme views and extreme situations share the same edge.
branches.cn: 极端观点与极端处境共享同一条边缘。

intro.en: Extreme comes from the Latin exterus family and has a large modern word family.
intro.cn: extreme 来自拉丁语 exterus 词族，现代词族很大。

latinIntro.en: Latin extremus and exterus are the source forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 extremus 与 exterus 是来源形式。

items.meaning: the furthest end or a severe situation
items.example: The injury affected the lower extremity.

items.exampleCN: 政府反对暴力极端主义。

items.example: The group was led by an extremist.
items.exampleCN: 这个团体由一名极端分子领导。

items.meaning: the opposite ends of a range
items.exampleCN: 气候在两个极端之间摆动。
极限运动吸引勇敢的人。

latinEntries.example: Extra is related to the same family.

definition_zh: 住宅的；居住的
definition_en: consisting of homes rather than shops or factories
core_image: 一排排房子、草坪和信箱，没有厂房和店铺
scene: 这片区域全是住宅街道，夜里安静得只听见风声。 The area is made up of residential streets that grow silent at night.
sceneCN: 这里 residential 是「住宅的」（第 1 个义项：由住宅构成的）；句意：这片区域全是住宅街道，夜里安静得只听见风声。

senses.title: Consisting of homes
senses.definition: made up of houses where people live rather than businesses
senses.definitionCN: 由人们居住的房屋构成，而非商业场所
senses.example: They live in a quiet residential area.
senses.exampleCN: 他们住在一个安静的住宅区。
senses.why: The -ial adjective describes an area whose purpose is residence.
senses.whyCN: -ial 形容词描述以居住为目的的区域。

senses.title: Involving living on site
senses.definition: connected with living in a place while studying or receiving care
senses.definitionCN: 与在学习或接受照护期间住在某处有关
senses.example: The college offers residential courses in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学院在夏季开设住宿课程。
senses.why: The word extends from homes to institutions where people also live.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从家庭扩展到人们同样居住的机构。

senses.title: Used for housing
senses.definition: designed or used as housing rather than for another purpose
senses.definitionCN: 设计或用作住房，而非其他用途
senses.example: Residential buildings line both sides of the road.
senses.exampleCN: 道路两旁都是住宅楼。
senses.why: Any building can be classified by whether it is meant for living in.
senses.whyCN: 任何建筑都可按是否用于居住来分类。

intro.en: Residential is residence plus the adjective ending -ial, from Latin residentia, a dwelling.
intro.cn: residential 是 residence 加形容词词尾 -ial，源于拉丁语 residentia（居所）。

items.en: Sedere means to sit.
items.cn: sedere 意为坐。

items.en: Residere means to remain or dwell.
items.cn: residere 意为留下、居住。

items.en: Residentia means a dwelling.
items.cn: residentia 意为居所。

items.en: Residence means a place of dwelling.
items.cn: residence 意为居住之处。

items.en: Residential forms the adjective for areas of homes.
items.cn: 到 19 世纪，residential 构成描述住宅区域的形容词。

items.en: Modern English uses residential for areas, buildings, and care.
items.cn: 现代英语中，residential 用于区域、建筑与照护。

note.en: Residential is the adjective of residence, and it sits near its family and near words for housing and suburbs.
note.cn: residential 是 residence 的形容词，与自身词族以及表示住房和郊区的词相邻。

entries.definition: a person who lives in a place
a home
to live in a place
relating to an area outside a city centre
relating to the home
buildings in which people live

normalIntro.en: Residential adds -ial to resident: describing an area made of homes.
normalIntro.cn: residential 在 resident 后加 -ial：描述由住宅构成的区域。

normal.en: Residential area is the most common phrase.
normal.cn: residential area 是最常见的短语。

normal.en: Residential streets have houses, not factories.
normal.cn: 住宅街道上是房屋，而不是工厂。

normal.en: Residential care means living in a care home.
normal.cn: residential care 指住在护理机构中。

normal.en: Residential property is housing rather than offices.
normal.cn: 住宅房产是住房而非办公场所。

normal.en: Compare suburban: suburban describes location, while residential describes use.
normal.cn: 对比 suburban：suburban 描述位置，residential 描述用途。

abstract.en: Picture rows of mailboxes and trimmed lawns.
abstract.cn: 想象一排排信箱和修剪整齐的草坪。

abstract.en: Imagine curtains closing one by one at dusk.
abstract.cn: 想象黄昏时窗帘一扇接一扇拉上。

abstract.en: Think of a street with no shop signs at all.
abstract.cn: 想象一条完全没有店铺招牌的街。

examples.en: They live in a quiet residential area.
examples.cn: 他们住在一个安静的住宅区。

examples.en: The college offers residential courses in summer.
examples.cn: 这所学院在夏季开设住宿课程。

examples.en: Residential buildings line both sides of the road.
examples.cn: 道路两旁都是住宅楼。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「resident + ial」——满是住户的地方，就是住宅区；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sedere（坐）→ residere（留下、居住）→ residentia（居所）→ residence ＋ -ial → residential。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective classifies places by living: a neighbourhood of homes, a course where students live in, and a building meant for housing.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个形容词按「居住」给场所分类：由住宅构成的街区、学生住校的课程，以及用于住房的建筑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rows of homes with lawns and letterboxes, no shop signs.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排排带草坪和信箱的住宅，没有店铺招牌。

branches.en: An area of homes is the main modern sense.
branches.cn: 住宅区域，是现代主要义项。

branches.en: Living in while studying or receiving care extends the idea.
branches.cn: 在学习或照护期间居住，扩展了这一概念。

branches.en: A building used for housing is residential property.
branches.cn: 用作住房的建筑就是住宅房产。

branches.en: Areas and individual buildings can both be residential.
branches.cn: 区域与单栋建筑都可以是住宅性的。

branches.en: Institutions and buildings both provide space for living.
branches.cn: 机构与建筑都提供居住空间。

intro.en: Residential is an English -ial adjective built on residence, from the Latin verb for remaining.
intro.cn: residential 是建立在 residence 上的英语 -ial 形容词，源于表示「留下」的拉丁动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin sedere means to sit and residentia means a dwelling; French residence carries the noun onward.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sedere 意为坐，residentia 意为居所；法语 residence 把这个名词继续传递。

items.example: Re- adds the sense of remaining.

definition_zh: 好看的；有魅力的；有吸引力的（条件、提议）
definition_en: pleasant to look at, or good enough to make people want it
core_image: 橱窗里的一件东西让人走过又退回来多看一眼
scene: 中介带人看房，一进门就被落地窗外的景色吸引。 The flat is small but very attractive.
sceneCN: 这里 attractive 是「好看的、有魅力的」（第 1 个义项）；句意是这套公寓不大，但非常讨人喜欢。

pos.zh: 形容词：好看的；有吸引力的

senses.title: Pleasing to look at
senses.definition: pleasant in appearance, so that people enjoy looking at you or it
senses.definitionCN: 外表讨人喜欢，让人愿意多看
senses.example: She wore a simple but attractive dress.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿了一条简单却很好看的连衣裙。
senses.why: The word describes the effect on the viewer: something attractive draws the eye before any judgment is made about it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词描述的是看的人受到的影响：有魅力的东西先抓住目光，人才会去评判它。

senses.title: Worth accepting
senses.definition: good enough to make people want to accept it or join in
senses.definitionCN: 条件足够好，让人愿意接受或参与
senses.example: They made us an attractive offer.
senses.exampleCN: 他们给了我们一个很有吸引力的报价。
senses.why: The pull is no longer visual but practical: a price, a job or a deal can attract a person just as a face can.
senses.whyCN: 这里的吸引力不再是视觉上的，而是实际利益上的：价格、工作或交易也像面容一样能把人拉过来。

intro.en: Attractive simply means having the power to draw.
intro.cn: attractive 的意思就是「具有拉过来的力量」。

items.en: trahere meant 'to draw or pull'.
items.cn: trahere 意为「拉、牵引」。

items.en: attractus was the participle 'drawn toward'.
items.cn: attractus 是表示「被拉近」的分词。

items.en: attractivus described something with power to draw.
items.cn: attractivus 描述「具有吸引力」的东西。

items.en: French attractif carried the adjective into English.
items.cn: 法语 attractif 把这个形容词带进英语。

items.en: English widened it from physical pull to beauty and good deals.
items.cn: 英语把它从物理拉力扩展到美貌与划算的条件。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that sound close; the near-meaning group holds words of beauty and appeal.
note.cn: 形近组是读音相近的词；近义组是表示美貌与吸引力的词。

entries.definition: paying close attention
to regard as the cause
to draw people toward
pleasant and inviting
delightful in manner or look
pleasant in appearance

normalIntro.en: Anything that draws people can be called attractive, from a face to a salary.
normalIntro.cn: 凡是能把人吸引过来的，从面容到薪水，都可以叫 attractive。

normal.en: The ending -ive makes it an adjective describing what does the attracting.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ive 使它成为形容词，描述发出吸引力的那一方。

normal.en: Use attractive to before the person or group being drawn.
normal.cn: 用 attractive to 引出被吸引的人或群体。

normal.en: An attractive offer is about terms, not looks.
normal.cn: attractive offer 说的是条件，不是长相。

normal.en: The noun is attraction and the verb is attract.
normal.cn: 名词是 attraction，动词是 attract。

normal.en: Do not mix it up with attentive, which means watching closely.
normal.cn: 不要与 attentive 混淆，后者意为专心留意。

abstract.en: See a shop window that stops people in the middle of a step.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇橱窗让人走到一半就停下来。

abstract.en: See a price tag that makes a buyer smile.
abstract.cn: 想象一个价签让买家笑起来。

abstract.en: See a face turn a whole room without a word.
abstract.cn: 想象一张脸一句话不说就让整个房间转过头来。

examples.en: The flat is small but very attractive.
examples.cn: 这套公寓不大，但非常讨人喜欢。

examples.en: She wore a simple but attractive dress.
examples.cn: 她穿了一条简单却很好看的连衣裙。

examples.en: They made us an attractive offer.
examples.cn: 他们给了我们一个很有吸引力的报价。

dict_mnemonic.text: attract 加 -ive：会把人拉过来的，就是有吸引力的；拉眼睛的是好看，拉钱包的是条件划算。

root: 源自拉丁语 attractivus「有吸引力的」，来自 attrahere「拉向」，词基 trahere 意为「拉」；经法语 attractif 进入英语，由物理拉力扩展到外貌与条件的吸引力。

sensesIntro.en: A beautiful face and a generous salary pull people in the same grammatical way.
sensesIntro.cn: 一张好看的脸和一份优厚的薪水，在语法上是以同一种方式把人拉过去的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shop window that makes a walker turn back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇橱窗让路人回头。

branches.en: an attractive dress
branches.cn: 好看的连衣裙

branches.en: an attractive smile
branches.cn: 迷人的微笑

branches.en: an attractive offer
branches.cn: 有吸引力的提议

branches.en: attractive to investors
branches.cn: 对投资者有吸引力

branches.en: physically attractive
branches.cn: 外表迷人

intro.en: The root tract, 'to draw', is the same one heard in attract and distraction.
intro.cn: 词根 tract 意为「拉」，在 attract 与 distraction 里听到的是同一个词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin trahere also gives tractor, traction and extract.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 trahere 还给出 tractor、traction 与 extract。

definition_zh: 反馈；反馈意见；（电子）回授
definition_en: comments on how well something works, information returned by a system, or a return of part of an electronic signal
core_image: 试讲结束后，同事们把写满建议的纸一张张递到他手里
scene: 试讲结束后，同事们逐条写下建议交给他。 The teacher welcomed feedback from her students.
sceneCN: 这里 feedback 是「反馈意见」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这位老师欢迎学生们的反馈。

senses.title: Comments on performance
senses.definition: comments about how well someone or something has done
senses.definitionCN: 关于某人或某事表现如何的意见
senses.example: The teacher gave feedback on each essay.
senses.exampleCN: 老师对每篇作文都给出了反馈。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense in learning and work.
senses.whyCN: 这是学习与工作中最常见的含义。

senses.title: Information from a system
senses.definition: information about the result of a process, used to adjust it
senses.definitionCN: 关于过程结果、用于调整该过程的信息
senses.example: The system uses feedback to adjust the temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 系统利用反馈来调节温度。
senses.why: Machines return information the way people return comments.
senses.whyCN: 机器返回信息，正如人返回意见。

senses.title: Electronic return
senses.definition: the return of part of an output signal to the input
senses.definitionCN: 把部分输出信号送回输入端
senses.example: Too much feedback caused a loud howl.
senses.exampleCN: 过强的回授引起了刺耳的啸叫。
senses.why: Audio equipment made the term famous.
senses.whyCN: 音响设备让这个术语广为人知。

intro.en: Feedback is an English compound of feed and back, first used in control engineering.
intro.cn: feedback 是 feed 与 back 的英语复合词，最初用于控制工程。

items.en: Fēdan meant to give food or supply.
items.cn: fēdan 意为给食物或供应。

items.en: Bæc meant the back or backward direction.
items.cn: bæc 意为背部或向后方向。

items.en: Engineers named the return of a signal feedback.
items.cn: 工程师把信号的返回称为 feedback。

items.en: The word spread to systems of control and communication.
items.cn: 该词扩展到控制与通信系统。

items.en: Feedback became common for comments on performance.
items.cn: feedback 成为表示表现评价的常用词。

note.en: Feedback is compared with similar-looking words and with words for responses.
note.cn: 把 feedback 与形近词以及表示回应的词作比较。

entries.definition: to give food
a bag of food for an animal
the rear part of something
a reply or reaction
a spoken or written remark
a response to something

normalIntro.en: Feedback is information fed back to the source so it can improve.
normalIntro.cn: feedback 是送回源头、帮助其改进的信息。

normal.en: Feedback is literally fed back to the sender.
normal.cn: feedback 字面上就是把信息「喂回」发送者。

normal.en: Positive feedback encourages more of the same.
normal.cn: 正面反馈会鼓励继续做同样的事。

normal.en: A feedback loop keeps adjusting itself.
normal.cn: 反馈回路会不断自我调节。

normal.en: Customer feedback shapes better products.
normal.cn: 顾客反馈塑造更好的产品。

normal.en: In audio, feedback can become a loud howl.
normal.cn: 在音响中，回授可能变成刺耳啸叫。

abstract.en: Feedback closes the circle between action and result.
abstract.cn: 反馈把行动与结果连成一个圆。

abstract.en: A system without feedback cannot correct itself.
abstract.cn: 没有反馈的系统无法自我纠错。

abstract.en: Praise and criticism are both information.
abstract.cn: 赞扬与批评都是一种信息。

examples.en: The teacher gave feedback on each essay.
examples.cn: 老师对每篇作文都给出了反馈。

examples.en: The system uses feedback to adjust the temperature.
examples.cn: 系统利用反馈来调节温度。

examples.en: We need more feedback from customers.
examples.cn: 我们需要更多顾客反馈。

dict_mnemonic.text: feedback 由 feed（送入）与 back（返回）组合而成，字面是「送回的信息」，先用于工程，后用于日常评价。

root: 由 feed（送入）与 back（返回）构成的英语复合词，核心义「返回源头的信息」。

sensesIntro.en: Feedback means comments on performance, information returned by a system, or electronic signal return.
sensesIntro.cn: feedback 意为表现评价、系统返回的信息，或电子信号回授。

core.en: A return of information that lets a system or person adjust.
core.cn: 让系统或个人得以调整的信息回流。

branches.en: Comments that help people improve.
branches.cn: 帮助人改进的意见。

branches.en: Information a system uses to adjust.
branches.cn: 系统用于调整的信息。

branches.en: Part of a signal returning to the input.
branches.cn: 部分信号返回输入端。

branches.en: People and machines both correct themselves with returned information.
branches.cn: 人与机器都依靠返回的信息自我修正。

branches.en: A howl in a microphone is feedback at its most literal.
branches.cn: 麦克风的啸叫是 feedback 最字面的形态。

intro.en: Feedback links the feed family with ideas of return and self-correction.
intro.cn: feedback 把 feed 词族与「返回、自我修正」的概念连接起来。

latinIntro.en: The word is a modern English compound, so Latin entries are not its direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 该词是现代英语复合词，拉丁条目并非其直接来源。

items.example: The lab recorded feedbacks from both systems.
items.exampleCN: 实验室记录了两个系统的反馈。

items.example: Sensors feed data to the computer.
items.exampleCN: 传感器向计算机输入数据。

items.example: The app feeds updates every minute.
items.exampleCN: 这个应用每分钟推送更新。

items.example: The feeding of data continues all night.

items.meaning: to feed power or data backward
items.example: The generator can backfeed the grid.
items.exampleCN: 发电机可以向电网反向馈电。
神经反馈用于训练注意力。
前馈可以提前防止错误。

definition_zh: 宽的；广阔的；概括的；浓重的
definition_en: wide from one side to the other
core_image: 一条宽阔平缓的河面
scene: 夕阳把水面照成金色。 A broad river ran past the town.
sceneCN: 这里 broad 是「宽的」（第 1 个义项：两侧之间距离大）；句意是一条宽阔的河从镇子旁流过。

senses.title: Wide from side to side
senses.definition: measuring a lot from one side to the other
senses.definitionCN: 从一侧到另一侧距离很大
senses.example: A broad river ran past the town.
senses.exampleCN: 一条宽阔的河从镇子旁流过。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, naming physical width.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，指物理上的宽度。

senses.title: Covering a large range
senses.definition: including many different things or areas
senses.definitionCN: 包含许多不同事物或领域
senses.example: She has broad interests in science and art.
senses.exampleCN: 她对科学和艺术都有广泛的兴趣。
senses.why: A wide space holds many things, so width became variety.
senses.whyCN: 宽阔的空间能容纳许多东西，宽度由此引申为多样性。

senses.title: General, not detailed
senses.definition: stated in general terms rather than in detail
senses.definitionCN: 只讲大概，不讲细节
senses.example: In broad terms, the plan will work.
senses.exampleCN: 大体上说，这个计划行得通。
senses.why: A view from wide above shows the outline, not the details.
senses.whyCN: 从高处远看只能看到轮廓，看不到细节。

intro.en: Broad is an Old English word for width that widened into range and generality.
intro.cn: broad 是古英语中表示宽度的词，后来扩展到范围与概括义。

items.en: brād described a wide surface or a wide road.
items.cn: brād 形容宽阔的表面或道路。

items.en: broad kept the physical sense and began to mean open or clear.
items.cn: broad 保留物理义，又开始表示开阔、清楚。

items.en: broad daylight named the open light of day.
items.cn: broad daylight 指大白天毫无遮掩的光。

items.en: broad terms described speech that stayed general.
items.cn: broad terms 指停留在概括层面的说法。

items.en: broad covers width, range and a strong accent.
items.cn: 如今 broad 兼指宽度、范围与浓重的口音。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the br- opening; the near-meaning group gives other words for width.
note.cn: 形近组都以 br- 开头；近义组是表示宽阔的词。

entries.definition: a flat piece of wood
in or to another country
a way for cars to travel on
large from side to side
covering a large area
extremely large in size

normalIntro.en: Broad is the width you see when a space opens out.
normalIntro.cn: broad 就是空间展开时你看到的宽度。

normal.en: A broad river is hard to cross.
normal.cn: 宽阔的河很难渡过。

normal.en: Broad shoulders carry heavy loads.
normal.cn: 宽肩能扛重物。

normal.en: The comparative is broader.
normal.cn: 比较级是 broader。

normal.en: Add -en to get the verb broaden.
normal.cn: 加 -en 得到动词 broaden。

normal.en: In broad terms means roughly.
normal.cn: in broad terms 的意思是大体上。

abstract.en: See a river too wide to shout across.
abstract.cn: 想象一条宽到喊不过去的河。

abstract.en: See a shoulder line squared and strong.
abstract.cn: 想象一条平直有力的肩线。

abstract.en: See a map viewed from far above.
abstract.cn: 想象从很高处俯看一张地图。

examples.en: A broad river ran past the town.
examples.cn: 一条宽阔的河从镇子旁流过。

examples.en: She has broad interests in science and art.
examples.cn: 她对科学和艺术都有广泛的兴趣。

examples.en: In broad terms, the plan will work.
examples.cn: 大体上说，这个计划行得通。

dict_mnemonic.text: broad 里的 oa 读得长而开，像把两臂向两侧伸开，这个动作就是宽。

root: broad 源自古英语 brād，本指表面或道路的宽度，中古英语起引申为开阔、清楚，后来又有了「概括的」与「浓重的」两义。

sensesIntro.en: A physical width, a wide range of things, and a general way of speaking.
sensesIntro.cn: 一种物理宽度、一大片范围、一种概括的说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a river too wide to shout across.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条宽到喊不过去的河。

branches.en: a broad river
branches.cn: 宽阔的河流

branches.en: broad shoulders
branches.cn: 宽宽的肩膀

branches.en: broad interests
branches.cn: 广泛的兴趣

branches.en: in broad terms
branches.cn: 大体上说

branches.en: in broad daylight
branches.cn: 光天化日之下

intro.en: Broad builds verbs, adverbs and nouns with -en, -ly and -th.
intro.cn: broad 加 -en、-ly 与 -th 可构成动词、副词和名词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Old English; the Latin items below are related only in meaning.
latinIntro.cn: 词基来自古英语，下面的拉丁词只在意思上相关。

definition_zh: 预料；预期；提前行动；抢先；预先考虑并满足；预先支用
definition_en: to expect that something will happen and often act before it does, or to deal with a matter in advance
core_image: 在事情落下来之前，先把手伸到它要落的位置
scene: 机场到达厅里，接机的人举着牌子，早早就站到了出口边上。 We anticipate a busy holiday season and booked extra staff months ago.
sceneCN: 这里 anticipate 是「预料、预期」（第 1 个义项：预期某事将会发生）；句意为公司预料到假日旺季会很忙，几个月前就多订了人手。画面里有到达厅、举牌接机的人与行李车。

pos.zh: 及物动词：预料；预期；提前准备；抢先；预先支用

collocations.zh: 预先想到并满足某人的需要
预先想到别人要问的问题

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ion 构成，义为「预期；期望；预先行动」
由本词加 -ory 构成，义为「预先的；预期的」
由本词加 -ive 构成，义为「有预知倾向的；期待中的」
由否定前缀 un- 加过去分词构成，义为「未预料到的」

senses.title: To expect something will happen
senses.definition: to expect that something will happen, often based on signs or experience
senses.definitionCN: 预期某事将会发生，常以迹象或经验为依据
senses.example: Economists anticipate a slow recovery next year.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家预期明年会缓慢复苏。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to take beforehand', and expecting is already taking the future into your hands.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词本义是「事先拿到」，而「预期」本就是先把未来拿到手里。

senses.title: To act before someone else
senses.definition: to act before another person or group does, so as to gain an advantage
senses.definitionCN: 在他人或其他团体之前行动，以取得优势
senses.example: The company anticipated its rivals by launching the app first.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司抢先推出应用，占了对手的先机。
senses.why: If the future can be taken in advance, then acting first is simply taking it before anyone else reaches it.
senses.whyCN: 既然未来可以事先拿到，那么抢先行动不过是赶在别人伸手之前把它拿走。

senses.title: To see and meet a need in advance
senses.definition: to notice a need before it is expressed and satisfy it in advance
senses.definitionCN: 在某项需要被说出口之前就察觉并提前满足它
senses.example: A good host anticipates the guests' needs before they ask.
senses.exampleCN: 好的主人会在客人开口之前就想到并满足他们的需要。
senses.why: A need is a future request; meeting it early means answering the request before it is spoken.
senses.whyCN: 需要是尚未说出口的请求；提前满足它，就是在这句话说出之前先行回答。

senses.title: To use money or income in advance
senses.definition: to spend or use money, income, or profit before the time it is due
senses.definitionCN: 在款项到期之前就花掉或动用金钱、收入或利润
senses.example: He anticipated part of his salary to pay the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 他预支了一部分薪水来付房租。
senses.why: This is the Latin image at its most literal: drawing tomorrow's money into today's hand.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁意象最字面的用法：把明天的钱拉到今天的掌心里。

senses.title: To cause something to happen early
senses.definition: to make something happen earlier than it otherwise would
senses.definitionCN: 使某事比原本会发生的时刻更早发生
senses.example: The report anticipated the debate by a full week.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告把辩论足足提前了一周。
senses.why: Taking the future in advance can also drag it forward: the event arrives sooner because it was pulled.
senses.whyCN: 把未来事先拿到，也可以把它往前拖：事件之所以更早到来，是因为它被拉了过来。

intro.en: Anticipate is a straight Latin borrowing whose two halves still show: ante 'before' plus capere 'to take'.
intro.cn: anticipate 是直接从拉丁语借来的词，两半依然看得见：ante「在前」加 capere「拿取」。

items.en: The preposition and prefix ante meant 'before, in front of', and it also carried the idea of preference or priority.
items.cn: 介词兼前缀 ante 意为「在……之前、在……前面」，也带有「优先」的意味。

items.en: The verb capere meant 'to take, seize, grasp', and it is the source of a large family including capture and concept.
items.cn: 动词 capere 意为「拿、抓、握住」，是 capture、concept 等一大族词的来源。

items.en: Ante plus capere formed anticipare 'to take before, take up in advance, forestall', with the participle anticipatus.
items.cn: ante 与 capere 构成 anticipare「事先拿取、提前占用、先发制人」，其过去分词为 anticipatus。

items.en: English borrowed the word directly from Latin in the sixteenth century; the earliest English sense was 'to take or use beforehand'.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪直接从拉丁语借入这个词；最早的英语义项是「事先拿取或动用」。

items.en: The sense of expecting now dominates, while the older 'act first' sense survives mainly in business, sport, and military writing.
items.cn: 今天「预期」占主导，较早的「抢先行动」义主要保留在商业、体育与军事文字中。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the derived family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of looking ahead, differing in how certain the future is and how early one acts.
note.cn: 形近组收本词的派生一族；近义组收各种「往前看」的动词，未来有多确定、行动有多早各有不同。

entries.definition: The noun for the feeling or act of expecting something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「预期、期待」，指期待某事的心情或行为。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning done or felt in advance of something.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「预先的、提前的」，指在某事之前就做出或感受到。

entries.definition: The past participle used as an adjective: expected or awaited.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词作形容词，义为「被预期的、期盼中的」。

entries.definition: To think that something will probably happen, without necessarily acting on it.
entries.definitionCN: 认为某事很可能发生，但不一定据此行动，是最中性的「预期」。

entries.definition: To say in advance what will happen, especially from evidence or calculation.
entries.definitionCN: 依据证据或推算事先说出将会发生什么，偏重「断言未来」。

entries.definition: To see or know something before it happens, often through judgment.
entries.definitionCN: 在事情发生之前看出或知道，多凭判断力，带有「有先见」的意味。

entries.definition: To act before others so as to prevent their action.
entries.definitionCN: 抢先行动以阻止他人行动，比 anticipate 更强调「先占住」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two real Latin halves, the participle, and the frames the verb actually takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的两个拉丁语成分、分词形式，以及这个动词实际搭配的句式。

normal.en: ante plus capere: taking before the thing has even arrived.
normal.cn: ante 加 capere：在东西还没到就先拿住。

normal.en: The shared cap- root also gives capture and captive, all about taking hold.
normal.cn: 共同的 cap- 词根还生出 capture 与 captive，都与「抓住」有关。

normal.en: The everyday frame is anticipate problems or anticipate that something will happen.
normal.cn: 日常句式是 anticipate problems 或 anticipate that 加从句。

normal.en: Anticipation is the noun of the waiting feeling before an event.
normal.cn: anticipation 是名词，指事件到来之前那种等待的心情。

normal.en: Anticipated in a headline means the event people have been waiting for.
normal.cn: 标题里的 anticipated 指众人一直在等的那件事。

abstract.en: Picture a hand already open under a window before the dropped key reaches it.
abstract.cn: 想象钥匙还没落下，一只手已经在窗下摊开等着。

abstract.en: Picture a chess player moving a piece to the square the opponent will need two moves later.
abstract.cn: 想象棋手把棋子挪到对手两步之后才要用的那格。

abstract.en: Picture a host pouring tea before the guest has said the word thirsty.
abstract.cn: 想象客人还没说出「渴」字，主人已经把茶倒上。

examples.en: Nobody anticipated how quickly the small protest would grow.
examples.cn: 没有人预料到那场小规模抗议扩散得如此之快。

examples.en: She anticipated his question and had the figures ready.
examples.cn: 她预先想到了他的问题，把数字都备好了。

examples.en: The nurses anticipated the storm and moved the patients to the upper floor.
examples.cn: 护士们预见到暴风雨，提前把病人转移到了楼上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安提西陪他」——提前安顿好、陪着他等，就是预料在先

root: 拉丁语 ante（在前）+ capere（拿取）→ anticipare（事先拿取、抢先）；过去分词 anticipatus 进入英语。词义由「提前拿用」扩展为「预料」「抢先」「预先满足需要」，core image 始终是「手先伸到事情要落的位置」。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses move from knowing the future to acting on it: expect it, arrive before rivals, meet a need early, draw money forward, and even pull the event closer.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项从「知道未来」走到「对未来动手」：预期它、赶在对手之前、提前满足需要、把钱提前取出，甚至把事件本身拉近。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching out to where something has not yet fallen.
core.cn: 核心意象：手先伸到某物尚未落下的那个位置。

branches.en: THE EXPECTATION LINE: the future is known before it arrives.
branches.cn: 预期线：未来在到来之前就已被看见。

branches.en: THE RACE LINE: the same early reach becomes an advantage over rivals.
branches.cn: 抢先线：同样的提前伸手，变成对对手的优势。

branches.en: THE CARE LINE: the early reach is directed at another person's unspoken need.
branches.cn: 体贴线：提前伸出的手朝向他人尚未说出的需要。

branches.en: THE MONEY LINE: taking tomorrow's resources into today.
branches.cn: 钱款线：把明天的资源拉到今天。

branches.en: THE PULL LINE: the future event itself is dragged nearer.
branches.cn: 前拉线：未来事件本身被拖得更近。

intro.en: Anticipate keeps Latin ante and the cap- root, then adds English verb and noun suffixes.
intro.cn: anticipate 保留拉丁语的 ante 与 cap- 词根，再加上英语的动词与名词后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is transparent: ante, capere and the derived anticipare and anticipatio.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语这一族很清楚：ante、capere，以及由它们构成的 anticipare 与 anticipatio。

items.exampleCN: 它为 anticipate 提供了「在前」这一层意思。

items.example: It supplies the taking in anticipate.
items.exampleCN: 它为 anticipate 提供了「拿取」这一层意思。

items.meaning: the shared stem of the family
items.example: It appears in anticipation and anticipatory.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 anticipation 与 anticipatory 中。

forming the past tense and participle
items.meaningCN: 构成过去式与过去分词

latinEntries.exampleCN: 它是 anticipare 的前一半。

latinEntries.example: It is the second half of anticipare.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它是 anticipare 的后一半。

latinEntries.example: It is the direct source of the English verb.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它是这个英语动词的直接来源。

latinEntries.example: It stands behind the English anticipation.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它是英语 anticipation 背后的拉丁名词。
